title.en: Volume 28 Biographies 20: Shi Ning; Lu Teng; He Ruodun; Quan Jingxuan
title.raw: 卷28 列傳第20 史寧 陸騰 賀若敦 權景宣 Volume 28 Biographies 20: Shi Ning; Lu Teng; He Ruodun; Quan Jingxuan

sentences.zh: 史寧 陸騰 賀若敦 權景宣

translations.literal: Shi Ning; Lu Teng; He Ruodun; Quan Jingxuan
translations.idiomatic: Shi Ning; Lu Teng; He Ruodun; Quan Jingxuan

sentences.zh: 史寧字永和，建康

translations.literal: Shi Ning, styled Yonghe, was from Jiankang
translations.idiomatic: Shi Ning, styled Yonghe, came from Jiankang

translations.literal: (Yuan) [emended variant]
translations.idiomatic: [Textual note: Yuan]

sentences.zh: 〔表〕氏人也。

translations.literal: 〔Biao〕 [emended: Yuan] clan man.
translations.idiomatic: He was a man of the Yuan clan.

sentences.zh: 曾祖豫，仕沮渠氏為臨松令。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Yu served the Juqu clan as magistrate of Linsong.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Yu had served the Juqu as magistrate of Linsong.

sentences.zh: 魏平涼州，祖灌隨例遷於撫寧鎮，因家焉。

translations.literal: When Wei pacified Liangzhou, his grandfather Guan moved with the general resettlement to Funing Garrison and settled his family there.
translations.idiomatic: After Wei pacified Liangzhou, his grandfather Guan was relocated with the others to Funing Garrison, where the family made its home.

sentences.zh: 父遵，初為征虜府鎧曹參軍。

translations.literal: His father Zun at first served as armor-bureau adjutant in the Pacification of Barbarians headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zun began as armor-bureau adjutant in the Pacification of Barbarians headquarters.

sentences.zh: 屬杜洛周構逆，六鎮自相屠陷，遵遂率鄉里二千家奔恆州。

translations.literal: When Du Luozhou raised rebellion, the six garrisons turned on one another in slaughter, and Zun led two thousand households of his district to flee to Heng Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Du Luozhou rebelled and the six garrisons fell into mutual slaughter, Zun led two thousand local households to Heng Province.

sentences.zh: 其後恆州為賊所敗，遵復歸洛陽。

translations.literal: Later Heng Province was defeated by bandits, and Zun returned to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when bandits overran Heng Province, Zun fled back to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 拜樓煩郡守。

translations.literal: He was appointed prefect of Loufan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was made prefect of Loufan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 及寧著勳，追贈散騎常侍、征西大將軍、涼州刺史，諡曰貞。

translations.literal: When Ning achieved merit, Zun was posthumously enfeoffed as Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary, General Who Conquers the West, and Inspector of Liang Province, with the posthumous title Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: After Ning won distinction, Zun was posthumously honored as Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary, General Who Conquers the West, and Inspector of Liang Province, with the posthumous name Zhen.

sentences.zh: 寧少以軍功，拜別將。

translations.literal: Ning in youth, through military merit, was appointed Separate Commander.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Ning earned a separate command through battlefield service.

sentences.zh: 遷直閣將軍、都督，宿衛禁中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Direct Palace General and Area Commander, guarding the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Direct Palace General and area commander, posted to guard the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 尋加持節、征東將軍、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Soon he was further given the staff of authority, made General Who Conquers the East, and Golden Grandee of the Purple Dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he also received the staff of authority, the title General Who Conquers the East, and the rank Golden Grandee of the Purple Dawn.

sentences.zh: 賀拔勝為荊州刺史，寧以本官為勝軍司，率步騎一千，隨勝之部。

translations.literal: When Heba Sheng became Inspector of Jing Province, Ning in his original office served as Sheng's army marshal, leading one thousand infantry and cavalry in Sheng's train.
translations.idiomatic: When Heba Sheng became inspector of Jing, Ning stayed in his post as Sheng's army marshal at the head of a thousand foot and horse.

sentences.zh: 值荊蠻騷動，三鵶路絕，寧先驅平之。

translations.literal: When Jing barbarians were in turmoil and the Sanya road was cut, Ning went ahead as vanguard and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jing tribes rose and the Sanya route was blocked, Ning led the vanguard and restored order.

sentences.zh: 因撫慰蠻左，翕然降附，遂稅得馬一千五百匹供軍。

translations.literal: He then comforted the barbarian left wing, who submitted in unity, and levied one thousand five hundred horses for the army.
translations.idiomatic: He then pacified the tribal levies on the left, who submitted as one, and raised fifteen hundred horses for the army.

sentences.zh: 尋除南郢州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was removed and made Inspector of Nan'e Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed inspector of Nan'e.

sentences.zh: 及勝為大行臺，表寧為大都督。

translations.literal: When Sheng became Grand Commissioner, he memorialized that Ning be made Grand Area Commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Sheng became grand commissioner, he recommended Ning as grand area commander.

sentences.zh: 率步騎一萬攻梁下溠戍，破之，封武平縣伯，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: He led ten thousand infantry and cavalry to attack Liang's Xiachi garrison, broke it, and was enfeoffed as Baron of Wuping with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He led ten thousand foot and horse against the Liang garrison at Xiachi, took it, and was enfeoffed Baron of Wuping with five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 又攻拔梁齊興鎮等九城，獲戶二萬而還。

translations.literal: He also stormed and took nine strongpoints including Liang's Qixing Garrison, capturing twenty thousand households before returning.
translations.idiomatic: He also captured nine Liang posts, including Qixing Garrison, and brought back twenty thousand households.

sentences.zh: 未及論功，屬魏孝武西遷，東魏遣侯景率衆寇荊州，寧隨勝奔梁。

translations.literal: Before rewards could be discussed, Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, and Eastern Wei sent Hou Jing with troops to invade Jing; Ning followed Sheng in flight to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Before honors were settled, Emperor Xiaowu of Wei fled west while Eastern Wei sent Hou Jing against Jing; Ning followed Sheng into Liang territory.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝引寧至香磴前，謂之曰：「觀卿風表，終至富貴，我當使卿衣錦還。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang led Ning before the incense altar and said to him: "Judging your bearing, you will reach wealth and honor in the end; I shall let you return home in brocade.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang received Ning before the incense altar and said, "Your bearing promises wealth and rank; I mean to send you home in brocade.

sentences.zh: 」寧答曰：「臣世荷魏恩，位為列將，天長喪亂，本朝傾覆，不能北面逆賊，幸得息肩有道。

translations.literal: " Ning replied: "Your servant's house has long owed Wei grace, holding rank among the commanders; Heaven prolongs chaos, our court is overturned—I cannot turn north to join the rebel; it is fortune to rest my shoulders under a righteous ruler.
translations.idiomatic: " Ning answered, "My family has long owed Wei; I hold a commander's commission. Heaven prolongs the turmoil and our dynasty lies in ruins—I cannot face north to serve the rebel. It is already fortune to find rest under a righteous sovereign.

sentences.zh: 儻如明詔，欣幸實多。

translations.literal: If it accords with your bright decree, my gladness would indeed be great.
translations.idiomatic: If your gracious command allows it, my joy would be beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 」因涕泣橫流，梁武為之動容。

translations.literal: " Tears streamed across his face, and Liang Wu was moved.
translations.idiomatic: " Tears ran down his face, and Emperor Wu was moved.

sentences.zh: 在梁二年，勝乃與寧密圖歸計。

translations.literal: After two years in Liang, Sheng and Ning secretly plotted return.
translations.idiomatic: After two years in Liang, Sheng and Ning secretly planned their return.

sentences.zh: 寧曰：「朱异旣為梁主所信任，請往見之。

translations.literal: Ning said: "Zhu Yi is trusted by the Liang ruler; let me go see him.
translations.idiomatic: Ning said, "Zhu Yi enjoys the Liang ruler's trust—let me visit him.

sentences.zh: 」勝然其言。

translations.literal: " Sheng approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: " Sheng agreed.

sentences.zh: 寧乃見异，申以投分之言，微托思歸之意，辭氣雅至。

translations.literal: Ning then saw Yi, spoke of their old bond, and lightly entrusted his wish to return; his tone was refined to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Ning sought out Yi, spoke of their shared past, and hinted at his wish to go home in language of the finest courtesy.

sentences.zh: 异亦嗟挹，謂寧曰：「桑梓之思，其可忘懷？

translations.literal: Yi also sighed in admiration and said to Ning: "Thought of the old home—how can it be forgotten?
translations.idiomatic: Yi sighed with respect and told Ning, "Love of one's native place—who could forget it?

sentences.zh: 當為奏聞，必望遂所請耳。

translations.literal: I shall memorialize on your behalf; you may surely hope your request will be granted.
translations.idiomatic: I will report upward for you; your wish should surely be granted.

sentences.zh: 」未幾，梁主果許勝等歸。

translations.literal: " Before long the Liang ruler indeed permitted Sheng and the others to return.
translations.idiomatic: " Before long the Liang emperor allowed Sheng and his party to leave.

sentences.zh: 大統二年，寧自梁歸闕，進爵為侯，增邑三百戶。

translations.literal: In the second year of Datong, Ning returned from Liang to court, was advanced in rank to marquis, and his fief was increased by three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong year 2 Ning came back from Liang, was raised to marquis, and gained three hundred more households in his fief.

sentences.zh: 久之，遷車騎將軍、行涇州事。

translations.literal: After a long while he was transferred to General of the Chariots and Cavalry and acted as administrator of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he became General of the Chariots and Cavalry and acted as administrator of Jing.

sentences.zh: 時賊帥莫折後熾寇掠居民，寧率州兵與行原州事李賢討破之。

translations.literal: At that time the bandit chief Mozhe Houji was raiding the people; Ning led provincial troops with Li Xian, acting administrator of Yuan, and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel chief Mozhe Houji was plundering the countryside, Ning and Li Xian, acting administrator of Yuan, routed him with provincial forces.

sentences.zh: 轉通直散騎常侍、東義州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Regular Attendant of Unimpeded Access and Inspector of Eastern Yi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Regular Attendant of Unimpeded Access and inspector of Eastern Yi.

sentences.zh: 東魏亦以故胡梨苟為東義州刺史。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei also appointed the former Hu Ligo as inspector of Eastern Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei likewise named the former Hu Ligo inspector of Eastern Yi.

sentences.zh: 寧僅得入州，梨苟亦至，寧迎擊，破之，斬其洛安郡守馮善道。

translations.literal: Ning had barely entered the prefecture when Ligo also arrived; Ning met him in battle, defeated him, and beheaded his Lu'an commandery administrator Feng Shandao.
translations.idiomatic: Ning had scarcely taken the prefecture when Ligo appeared; Ning met and broke him, beheading his Lu'an commandery chief Feng Shandao.

sentences.zh: 州旣鄰接疆埸，百姓流移，寧留心撫慰，咸來復業。

translations.literal: The prefecture bordered the frontier and the people were displaced; Ning gave his heart to comfort them, and all came back to their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture lay on the border and the people had fled; Ning worked to reassure them until they returned to their fields.

sentences.zh: 十二年，轉涼州刺史。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was transferred to Inspector of Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: In year 12 he was transferred to inspector of Liang.

sentences.zh: 寧未至而前刺史宇文仲和據州作亂。

translations.literal: Before Ning arrived, the former inspector Yuwen Zhonghe held the province in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Before Ning arrived, the outgoing inspector Yuwen Zhonghe held the province in revolt.

sentences.zh: 詔遣獨孤信率兵與寧討之，寧先至涼州，為陳禍福，城中吏民皆相率降附。

translations.literal: An edict sent Dugu Xin with troops to join Ning in punishing him; Ning reached Liang first, explained fortune and ruin, and the city's officials and people all submitted in succession.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent Dugu Xin with an army; Ning reached Liang first, laid out the stakes, and the officials and people of the city submitted one after another.

sentences.zh: 仲和仍據城不下，尋亦克之。

translations.literal: Zhonghe still held the city and would not come down, but was soon taken.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonghe still held the walls, but was soon captured.

sentences.zh: 加車騎大將軍、儀同三司、大都督、涼西涼二州諸軍事、散騎常侍、涼州刺史。

translations.literal: He was given Grand General of the Chariots and Cavalry, Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, Grand Area Commander, military affairs of Liang and Western Liang, Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary, and Inspector of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He received the titles Grand General of the Chariots and Cavalry, Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, and grand area commander over Liang and Western Liang, with Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and inspector of Liang.

sentences.zh: 十五年，遷驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，加侍中，進爵為公。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was transferred to General of Agile Cavalry, Grand Master of the Palace with the same honors as the Three Dukes, with Attendant-in-Ordinary added, and advanced in rank to duke.
translations.idiomatic: In year 15 he became General of Agile Cavalry and Grand Master of the Palace with Three-Duke honors, was made attendant-in-ordinary, and advanced to duke.

sentences.zh: 十六年，宕昌叛羌獠甘作亂，逐其王彌定而自立，幷連結傍乞鐵怱及鄭五醜等，詔寧率軍與宇文貴、豆盧寧等討之。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year the rebellious Qiang and Liao of Dangchang, Liaogan, drove out their king Mideng and set themselves up, also linking with the neighboring Qie Tiecang and Zheng Wuchou; an edict ordered Ning to lead troops with Yuwen Gui, Dou Lu Ning, and others to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: In year 16 the rebel Qiang and Liao of Dangchang, Liaogan, expelled King Mideng and seized power, allying with Qie Tiecang and Zheng Wuchou nearby; Ning was ordered out with Yuwen Gui, Dou Lu Ning, and others.

sentences.zh: 寧別擊獠甘，而山路險阻，纔通單騎，獠甘已分其黨立柵守險。

translations.literal: Ning separately struck Liaogan; the mountain road was perilous and only a single horse could pass, yet Liaogan had already divided his party to build stockades and hold the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Ning struck at Liaogan on a separate route; the trail allowed only single file, yet Liaogan had already split his men to fortify the heights.

sentences.zh: 寧進兵攻之，遂破其柵。

translations.literal: Ning advanced to attack and broke their stockades.
translations.idiomatic: Ning pressed the attack and broke the stockades.

sentences.zh: 獠甘率三萬人逆戰，寧復大破之，追奔至宕昌。

translations.literal: Liaogan led thirty thousand men to meet him in battle; Ning again routed them and pursued to Dangchang.
translations.idiomatic: Liaogan met him with thirty thousand men; Ning defeated him again and chased the fugitives to Dangchang.

sentences.zh: 獠甘將百騎走投生羌鞏廉玉。

translations.literal: Liaogan led a hundred horsemen in flight to throw himself on the raw Qiang Gong Lianyu.
translations.idiomatic: Liaogan fled with a hundred riders to the raw Qiang chief Gong Lianyu.

sentences.zh: 彌定遂得復位。

translations.literal: Mideng thus regained his throne.
translations.idiomatic: Mideng was restored to his throne.

sentences.zh: 寧以未獲獠甘，密欲圖之，乃揚聲欲還。

translations.literal: Because Liaogan had not been taken, Ning secretly planned against him, and spread word that he intended to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Liaogan still at large, Ning feigned a withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 獠甘聞之，復招引叛羌，依山起柵，欲攻彌定。

translations.literal: When Liaogan heard this, he again gathered rebellious Qiang, built stockades on the mountains, and intended to attack Mideng.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, Liaogan rallied rebel Qiang, fortified the hills, and prepared to strike Mideng.

sentences.zh: 寧謂諸將曰：「此羌入吾術中，當進兵擒之耳。

translations.literal: Ning told the generals: "These Qiang have entered my trap; we should advance and seize them.
translations.idiomatic: Ning told his officers, "These Qiang have walked into my trap—we should advance and take them.

sentences.zh: 」諸將思歸，咸曰：「生羌聚散無常，依據山谷，今若追討，恐引日無成。

translations.literal: " The generals longed to return and all said: "Raw Qiang gather and scatter without rule, relying on valleys; if we pursue now, we fear days will pass without success.
translations.idiomatic: " The officers, eager to go home, objected: "The raw Qiang come and go at will along the ravines; pursuit may drag on without end.

sentences.zh: 且彌定還得守蕃，將軍功已立矣。

translations.literal: Moreover Mideng is back guarding the border tribes; the general's merit is already established.
translations.idiomatic: Mideng is back on his throne guarding the tribes; your merit is already made.

sentences.zh: 獠甘勢弱，彌定足能制之。

translations.literal: Liaogan's strength is weak; Mideng is fully able to control him.
translations.idiomatic: Liaogan is weak; Mideng can handle him.

sentences.zh: 以此還師，策之上者。

translations.literal: To withdraw the army on this basis is the best policy.
translations.idiomatic: Withdraw now—that is the superior plan.

sentences.zh: 」寧曰：「一日縱敵，數世之患，豈可舍將滅之寇，更煩再舉。

translations.literal: " Ning said: "To let the enemy go for a day is trouble for generations—how can we abandon a foe on the verge of destruction and trouble ourselves with a second campaign?
translations.idiomatic: " Ning said, "Spare an enemy for a day and your heirs pay for generations. How leave a foe about to perish and campaign again?

sentences.zh: 人臣之禮，知無不為。

translations.literal: The minister's duty is to act whenever he knows what must be done.
translations.idiomatic: A subject serves by doing what must be done.

sentences.zh: 以此諸君不足與計事也。

translations.literal: On this account you gentlemen are not fit to plan the affair.
translations.idiomatic: You are not fit to counsel on this matter.

sentences.zh: 如更沮衆，寧豈不能斬諸君邪！

translations.literal: If you obstruct the host again, can Ning not behead you gentlemen!
translations.idiomatic: Obstruct me again and I will behead every one of you!

sentences.zh: 」遂進軍，獠甘衆亦至，與戰，大破之，生獲獠甘，狥而斬之。

translations.literal: " He then advanced; Liaogan's host also came, and in battle he routed them greatly, took Liaogan alive, and executed him as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: " He marched on; Liaogan came out, was shattered, taken alive, and executed as a warning.

sentences.zh: 幷執鞏廉玉送闕。

translations.literal: He also seized Gong Lianyu and sent him to court.
translations.idiomatic: He seized Gong Lianyu as well and sent him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 所得軍實，悉分賞將士，寧無私焉。

translations.literal: Booty from the army was all divided to reward officers and soldiers; Ning took none for himself.
translations.idiomatic: He divided all captured goods among the troops and kept nothing for himself.

sentences.zh: 師還，詔寧率所部鎮河陽。

translations.literal: When the army returned, an edict ordered Ning to lead his command to garrison Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return he was ordered to garrison Heyang with his command.

sentences.zh: 寧先在涼州，戎夷服其威惠，遷鎮之後，邊民並思慕之。

translations.literal: Ning had earlier been in Liang Province, where the tribes submitted to his might and kindness; after he was transferred to garrison, the frontier people all yearned for him.
translations.idiomatic: In Liang Province the tribes had submitted to his authority and grace; after he left the border people missed him.

sentences.zh: 時突厥木汗可汗假道涼州，將襲吐渾，太祖令寧率騎隨之。

translations.literal: At that time the Türk Muhan Qaghan asked passage through Liang to strike Tuyuhun; the Grand Progenitor ordered Ning to lead cavalry and follow.
translations.idiomatic: When the Türk qaghan Muhan asked passage through Liang to attack Tuyuhun, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai ordered Ning to follow with cavalry.

sentences.zh: 軍至番禾，吐渾已覺，奔於南山。

translations.literal: The army reached Fanhe; Tuyuhun had already sensed them and fled to the southern mountains.
translations.idiomatic: At Fanhe the Tuyuhun had already sensed them and fled into the southern hills.

sentences.zh: 木汗將分兵追之，令俱會於青海。

translations.literal: Muhan was about to divide troops in pursuit and ordered all to meet at Qinghai.
translations.idiomatic: Muhan meant to split his forces in pursuit and rendezvous at Qinghai.

sentences.zh: 寧謂木汗曰：「樹敦、賀真二城，是吐渾巢穴。

translations.literal: Ning said to Muhan: "Shudun and Hezhen, the two cities, are Tuyuhun's nests.
translations.idiomatic: Ning told Muhan, "Shudun and Hezhen are the Tuyuhun heartland.

sentences.zh: 今若拔其本根，餘種自然離散，此上策也。

translations.literal: If we now uproot them, the remnant clans will naturally scatter—this is the upper stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Strike the root and the rest will scatter of themselves—that is the best plan.

sentences.zh: 」木汗從之，卽分為兩軍。

translations.literal: " Muhan followed this, and immediately divided into two armies.
translations.idiomatic: " Muhan agreed and split his force in two.

sentences.zh: 木汗從北道向賀真，寧趣樹敦。

translations.literal: Muhan took the northern road toward Hezhen; Ning hastened to Shudun.
translations.idiomatic: Muhan took the northern road toward Hezhen while Ning hurried to Shudun.

sentences.zh: 渾娑周國王率衆逆戰，寧擊斬之。

translations.literal: The Tuyuhun king of Suozhou led his host to meet him in battle; Ning struck and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: The Suozhou king of Tuyuhun met him in force; Ning killed him in battle.

sentences.zh: 踰山履險，遂至樹敦。

translations.literal: Crossing mountains and treading peril, he then reached Shudun.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed mountains and dangerous ground until he reached Shudun.

sentences.zh: 敦是渾之舊都，多諸珍藏。

translations.literal: Dun was the old capital of Hun; it held many stored treasures.
translations.idiomatic: Shudun was the old capital, rich in stored treasure.

sentences.zh: 而渾主先已奔賀真，留其征南王及數千人固守。

translations.literal: The Tuyuhun ruler had already fled to Hezhen, leaving his Prince Who Conquers the South and several thousand men to hold firm.
translations.idiomatic: The Tuyuhun king had already fled to Hezhen, leaving his Prince Who Conquers the South with a few thousand men to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 寧進兵攻之，退，渾人果開門逐之，因回兵奮擊，門未及闔，寧兵遂得入。

translations.literal: Ning advanced to attack, then withdrew; the Tuyuhun men indeed opened the gate to drive him off, and he wheeled back in fierce assault—before the gate could close, Ning's troops entered.
translations.idiomatic: Ning attacked, then feigned retreat; the defenders opened the gates to chase him, and he wheeled back so hard the gates never shut—his men poured in.

sentences.zh: 生獲其征南王，俘虜男女、財寶，盡歸諸突厥。

translations.literal: He took alive the Prince Who Conquers the South; male and female captives and valuables all went to the Türks.
translations.idiomatic: He captured the Prince Who Conquers the South alive; people and plunder all passed to the Türks.

sentences.zh: 渾賀羅拔王依險為柵，周回五十餘里，欲塞寧路。

translations.literal: The Tuyuhun Heluoba king relied on the passes and made a stockade of more than fifty li in circuit, intending to block Ning's road.
translations.idiomatic: King Heluoba of Tuyuhun fortified a fifty-li stockade in the defiles to block Ning's path.

sentences.zh: 寧攻其柵，破之，俘斬萬計，獲雜畜數萬頭。

translations.literal: Ning attacked the stockade and broke it, capturing and killing tens of thousands, and taking tens of thousands of head of mixed livestock.
translations.idiomatic: Ning stormed the stockade, killed tens of thousands, and took tens of thousands of mixed livestock.

sentences.zh: 木汗亦破賀真，虜渾主妻子，大獲珍物。

translations.literal: Muhan also broke Hezhen, captured the Tuyuhun ruler's wife and children, and gained great treasures.
translations.idiomatic: Muhan likewise took Hezhen, seized the Tuyuhun king's family, and won great treasure.

sentences.zh: 寧還軍於青海，與木汗會。

translations.literal: Ning returned his army to Qinghai and met Muhan.
translations.idiomatic: Ning marched back to Qinghai and joined Muhan.

sentences.zh: 木汗握寧手，歎其勇決，幷遺所乘良馬，令寧於帳前乘之，木汗親自步送。

translations.literal: Muhan clasped Ning's hand, sighed at his bold resolve, and also gave the fine horse he himself rode, ordering Ning to mount before the tent while Muhan walked alongside to see him off.
translations.idiomatic: Muhan took his hand, praised his daring, gave him his own fine horse, had him mount before the tent, and walked beside him as escort.

sentences.zh: 突厥以寧所圖必破，皆畏憚之，咸曰：「此中國神智人也。

translations.literal: The Türks, because Ning's plans always succeeded, all feared him and said: "This is a divine man of China.
translations.idiomatic: The Türks, seeing his plans always succeed, feared him and said, "This Chinese man has the wisdom of a god.

sentences.zh: 」及將班師，木汗又遺寧奴婢一百口、馬五百匹、羊一萬口。

translations.literal: " When he was about to withdraw the army, Muhan again gave Ning one hundred male and female slaves, five hundred horses, and ten thousand sheep.
translations.idiomatic: " As the army withdrew, Muhan gave him a hundred slaves, five hundred horses, and ten thousand sheep.

sentences.zh: 寧乃還州。

translations.literal: Ning then returned to his province.
translations.idiomatic: Ning then returned to his post.

sentences.zh: 尋被徵入朝，屬太祖崩，寧悲慟不已，乃請赴陵所盡哀，幷告行師克捷。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned to court; when the Grand Progenitor died, Ning grieved without end, requested to go to the tomb precinct to fulfill mourning, and reported the army's victories on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was called to court; when Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai died, Ning mourned deeply, asked to mourn at the tomb, and reported his victories in the field.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，拜小司徒，出為荊襄淅郢等五十二州及江陵鎮防諸軍事、荊州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, Ning was appointed Lesser Minister of Works and sent out as military commander of fifty-two prefectures including Jing, Xiang, and Xi, with defense of Jiangling, and Inspector of Jing.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin succeeded, Ning became Lesser Minister of Works and commander over fifty-two prefectures including Jing, Xiang, and Xi, with Jiangling and the inspectorate of Jing.

sentences.zh: 寧有識畫，諳兵權，臨敵指撝，皆如其策，甚得當時之譽。

translations.literal: Ning had insight and design, understood military authority; facing the enemy his commands all matched his plans, and he won the praise of the age.
translations.idiomatic: He had strategic vision and grasp of command; in battle his orders matched his plans, and his fame stood high in his day.

sentences.zh: 及在荊州，頗自奢縱貪濁，不修法度。

translations.literal: When he was in Jing Province he was quite self-indulgent, greedy and corrupt, and did not repair the laws.
translations.idiomatic: In Jing he grew extravagant and corrupt and let the law slide.

sentences.zh: 嘗出，有人訴州佐曲法，寧還付被訟者治之。

translations.literal: Once when he went out, someone accused a provincial aide of bending the law; Ning handed the accuser back to the accused for punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Once, when someone complained that a provincial aide had broken the law, Ning returned the complainant to the accused for punishment.

sentences.zh: 自是有事者不復敢言，聲名大損於西州。

translations.literal: From then on those with grievances no longer dared speak, and his reputation was greatly damaged in the western provinces.
translations.idiomatic: After that no one dared bring a grievance, and his name suffered greatly in the west.

sentences.zh: 保定三年，卒於州。

translations.literal: In the third year of Baoding he died in the province.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoding year 3 he died in office.

sentences.zh: 諡曰烈。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Lie.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous name was Lie.

sentences.zh: 子雄嗣。

translations.literal: His son Xiong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiong succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 雄字世武。

translations.literal: Xiong, styled Shiwu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong, styled Shiwu.

sentences.zh: 少勇敢，膂力過人，便弓馬，有算略。

translations.literal: In youth he was brave, his physical strength surpassing other men; skilled with bow and horse, he had calculation and design.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was fearless, stronger than other men, expert with bow and horse, and sharp in counsel.

sentences.zh: 年十四，從寧於牽屯山奉迎太祖。

translations.literal: At age fourteen he followed Ning to Qiantun Mountain to welcome the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen he went with Ning to Qiantun Mountain to welcome Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai.

sentences.zh: 仍從校獵，弓無虛發。

translations.literal: He also followed on the hunt; his bow never missed.
translations.idiomatic: On the hunt his bow never missed.

sentences.zh: 太祖歎異之。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor sighed in wonder at him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai marveled at him.

sentences.zh: 尋尚太祖女永富公主。

translations.literal: Soon he married the Grand Progenitor's daughter, Princess Yongfu.
translations.idiomatic: He soon married Princess Yongfu, the Grand Progenitor's daughter.

sentences.zh: 除使持節、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，累遷駕部中大夫、大馭中大夫。

translations.literal: He was appointed Bearer of the Staff, General of Agile Cavalry, and Grand Master of the Palace with the same honors as the Three Dukes, and successively rose to Director of the Chariot Office and Director of the Great Horse Office.
translations.idiomatic: He received the staff of authority, General of Agile Cavalry, and Three-Duke honors, then rose through the chariot and horse directorates.

sentences.zh: 從柱國、枹罕公辛威鎮金城，遂卒於軍，時年二十四。

translations.literal: Following the pillar-of-state, Duke of Baohan Xin Wei in garrison at Jincheng, he died in the army at age twenty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Duke of Baohan Xin Wei to garrison Jincheng and died in camp at twenty-four.

sentences.zh: 雄弟祥，以父勳賜爵武遂縣公。

translations.literal: Xiong's younger brother Xiang, through his father's merit, was granted the title Duke of Wusui County.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong's brother Xiang inherited a county dukedom for their father's service.

sentences.zh: 祥弟雲，亦以父勳賜爵武平縣公，歷位司織下大夫，儀同大將軍。

translations.literal: Xiang's younger brother Yun, also through his father's merit, was granted Duke of Wuping County, and held office as Director of Weaving, Lower Grade, and General Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Another brother, Yun, was made Duke of Wuping for their father's merit and served as weaving director and general of Three-Duke rank.

sentences.zh: 雲弟威，亦以父勳賜爵武當縣公。

translations.literal: Yun's younger brother Wei, also through his father's merit, was granted Duke of Wudang County.
translations.idiomatic: Yun's brother Wei likewise received Wudang county for their father's deeds.

sentences.zh: 陸騰字顯聖，代人也。

translations.literal: Lu Teng, styled Xiansheng, was a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Teng, styled Xiansheng, came from Dai.

sentences.zh: 高祖俟，魏征西大將軍、東平王。

translations.literal: His high ancestor Hou served Wei as General Who Conquers the West and Prince of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: His forebear Hou had been Wei's General Who Conquers the West and Prince of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 祖彌，夏州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Mi was Inspector of Xia Province.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Mi was inspector of Xia.

sentences.zh: 父旭，性雅澹，好《老易》緯候之學，撰《五星要訣》及《兩儀真圖》，頗得其指要，太和中，徵拜中書博士，稍遷散騎常侍。

translations.literal: His father Xu by nature was refined and detached, fond of the Laozi, Changes, and apocryphal studies; he wrote Essentials of the Five Stars and the True Chart of the Two Poles, grasping their essentials well; in the Taihe era he was summoned as Doctor of the Secretariat and gradually rose to Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xu was quiet and scholarly, devoted to the Laozi, the Changes, and omen lore; he wrote on the five stars and the two poles with real insight, entered service in Taihe as a secretariat doctor, and rose to regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 知天下將亂，遂隱於太行山。

translations.literal: Seeing the realm would fall into chaos, he hid on Mount Taihang.
translations.idiomatic: Foreseeing chaos, he withdrew to Mount Taihang.

sentences.zh: 孝莊卽位，屢徵不起。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozhuang took the throne, he was repeatedly summoned but would not come.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozhuang summoned him repeatedly; he refused.

sentences.zh: 後贈幷汾恆肆四州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was posthumously given the four provinces Bing, Fen, Heng, and Si.
translations.idiomatic: He was later posthumously honored over Bing, Fen, Heng, and Si.

sentences.zh: 騰少慷慨有大節，解巾員外散騎侍郎、司徒府中兵參軍。

translations.literal: Teng in youth was bold and had great integrity; he doffed the scarf as Outer Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and army adjutant in the Secretariat headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Young Teng was ardent and high-minded, beginning as outer attendant and secretariat army adjutant.

sentences.zh: 爾朱榮入洛，以騰為通直散騎侍郎、帳內都督。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong entered Luoyang, he made Teng Regular Attendant of Unimpeded Access and commander of the inner guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong took Luoyang, Teng became unimpeded attendant and inner-guard commander.

sentences.zh: 從平葛榮，以功賜爵清河縣伯。

translations.literal: Following the pacification of Ge Rong, through merit he was granted Baron of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: After Ge Rong was crushed he was made Baron of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 普泰初，遷朱衣直閤。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Putai he was transferred to Scarlet-Robe Direct Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Putai he joined the scarlet-robed palace guard.

sentences.zh: 尚安平主，卽東萊王貴平女也。

translations.literal: He married the Lady of Peace and Stability, daughter of Prince Gui of Donglai.
translations.idiomatic: His wife was the Lady of Peace and Stability, daughter of Prince Gui of Donglai.

sentences.zh: 魏孝武幸貴平第，見騰，與語悅之，謂貴平曰：「阿翁真得好婿。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu of Wei visited Gui's residence, saw Teng, spoke with him and was pleased, and said to Gui: "Sir, you truly have a fine son-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu visited Gui's house, met Teng, enjoyed their talk, and told Gui, "You have found an excellent match.

sentences.zh: 」卽擢為通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: " He was immediately promoted to Regular Attendant of Unimpeded Access.
translations.idiomatic: " Teng was at once made Regular Attendant of Unimpeded Access.

sentences.zh: 及孝武西遷，騰時使青州，遂沒於鄴。

translations.literal: When Xiaowu moved west, Teng was then on mission to Qing Province and was stranded in Ye.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaowu fled west, Teng was on mission in Qing and was trapped in Ye.

sentences.zh: 東魏興和初，徵拜征西將軍，領陽城郡守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Eastern Wei's Xinghe era he was summoned as General Who Conquers the West and made administrator of Yangcheng Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Eastern Wei's Xinghe opening he was called back as General Who Conquers the West and Yangcheng commandery chief.

sentences.zh: 大統九年，大軍東討，以騰所據沖要，遂先攻之。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Datong the great army campaigned east; because Teng held a vital point, he was attacked first.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong year 9 the main army marched east and struck Teng first because his post was critical.

sentences.zh: 時兵威甚盛，長史麻休勸騰降，不許，拒守經月餘，城陷被執。

translations.literal: Military might was then very strong; Chief Clerk Ma Xiu urged Teng to surrender, but he would not, held out for more than a month, and when the city fell was taken prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: The besiegers were overwhelming; Ma Xiu urged surrender, but Teng refused, held out over a month, and was captured when the walls fell.

sentences.zh: 太祖釋而禮之，問其東間消息，騰盛陳東州人物，又敘述時事，辭理抑揚。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor released and honored him, asked news of the east, and Teng fully described the men of the eastern provinces and narrated current affairs with rising and falling rhetoric.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai freed and honored him, asked about the east, and Teng spoke at length of eastern worthies and the times with eloquent balance.

sentences.zh: 太祖笑曰：「卿真不背本也。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor laughed and said: "You truly do not betray your roots.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Progenitor laughed and said, "You have not forgotten where you came from.

sentences.zh: 」卽拜帳內大都督。

translations.literal: " He was immediately appointed Grand Commander of the Inner Guard.
translations.idiomatic: " He was made grand commander of the inner guard at once.

sentences.zh: 未幾，除太子庶子，遷武衛將軍。

translations.literal: Before long he was made Crown Prince's Household Assistant and transferred to Guard General of Wuwei.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became crown prince's assistant and then Guard General of Wuwei.

sentences.zh: 旣為太祖所知，願立功效，不求內職，太祖嘉之。

translations.literal: Once known to the Grand Progenitor, he wished to establish merit and did not seek inner posts; the Grand Progenitor praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Known to the Grand Progenitor, he asked for field command rather than court office, and was praised for it.

sentences.zh: 十三年，拜車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was appointed General of the Chariots and Cavalry and Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: In year 13 he became General of the Chariots and Cavalry with Three-Duke honors.

sentences.zh: 魏廢帝元年，安康賊黃衆寶等作亂，連結漢中，衆數萬，攻圍東梁州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Emperor Fei of Wei the Ankang bandit Huang Zhongbao and others rebelled, linking with Hanzhong, their host numbering tens of thousands, besieging Eastern Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: In Wei Emperor Fei year 1 the Ankang rebel Huang Zhongbao joined Hanzhong forces numbering tens of thousands and besieged Eastern Liang.

sentences.zh: 城中糧盡，詔騰率軍自子午穀以援之。

translations.literal: Grain in the city was exhausted; an edict ordered Teng to lead troops through Ziwu Valley to relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: When the city ran out of grain, Teng was ordered through Ziwu Valley with relief.

sentences.zh: 騰乃星言就道，至便與戰，大破之。

translations.literal: Teng marched by forced stages; on arrival he fought at once and routed them greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Teng forced the march, fought on arrival, and broke them decisively.

sentences.zh: 軍還，拜龍州刺史，太祖謂騰曰：「今欲通江

translations.literal: When the army returned he was made Inspector of Long Province; the Grand Progenitor said to Teng: "Now I wish to open the river route to Jiang
translations.idiomatic: On return he was made inspector of Long; the Grand Progenitor told him, "I mean to open the river route south

translations.literal: (You) [emended variant]
translations.idiomatic: [Textual note: You route]

sentences.zh: 〔油〕路，直出南

translations.literal: 〔Oil〕 [emended: You] road, to go straight out to southern
translations.idiomatic: the You route straight into southern

translations.literal: (Zou) [emended variant]
translations.idiomatic: [Textual note: Zou]

sentences.zh: 〔秦〕，卿宜善思經略。

translations.literal: 〔Qin〕 [emended: Zou]—you should think well on strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Qin—you must plan the campaign carefully.

sentences.zh: 」騰曰：「必望臨機制變，未敢預陳。

translations.literal: " Teng said: "I surely hope to adapt at the moment; I dare not state it beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: " Teng said, "I will adapt when the moment comes—I dare not lay out plans in advance.

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「此是卿取柱國之日，卿其勉之。

translations.literal: " The Grand Progenitor said: "This is the day you win your pillar-of-state rank; exert yourself.
translations.idiomatic: " The Grand Progenitor said, "This is how you earn your pillar-of-state rank—do your utmost.

sentences.zh: 」卽解所服金帶賜之。

translations.literal: " He immediately removed the golden belt he wore and gave it to him.
translations.idiomatic: " He gave Teng the golden belt from his own waist.

sentences.zh: 州民李廣嗣、李武等憑據岩險，以為堡壁，招集不逞之徒，攻劫郡縣，歷政不能治。

translations.literal: The provincials Li Guangsi and Li Wu relied on cliffs and ravines as fortresses, gathered lawless men, raided commanderies and counties, and successive administrations could not pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangsi and Li Wu held the cliffs, rallied outlaws, and raided the districts until no governor could control them.

sentences.zh: 騰密令多造飛梯，身率麾下，夜往掩襲，未明，四面俱上，遂破之，執廣嗣等於鼓下。

translations.literal: Teng secretly ordered many scaling ladders made, personally led his men in a night assault, and before dawn attackers rose on all four sides, broke them, and seized Guangsi and the others below the drum platform.
translations.idiomatic: Teng had scaling ladders built in secret, led a night assault at dawn from all sides, broke the stronghold, and dragged Guangsi and Wu before the drums.

sentences.zh: 其黨有任公忻者，更聚徒衆，圍逼州城。

translations.literal: Among their party was one Ren Gongxin, who again gathered followers and besieged the provincial city.
translations.idiomatic: Their follower Ren Gongxin rallied another host and besieged the provincial capital.

sentences.zh: 乃語騰曰：「但免廣嗣及武，卽散兵請罪。

translations.literal: He then said to Teng: "Only spare Guangsi and Wu and I will disband and beg punishment.
translations.idiomatic: He told Teng, "Spare only Guangsi and Wu and I will disband and submit.

sentences.zh: 」騰謂將士曰：「吾若不殺廣嗣等，可謂隳軍實而長寇讐，事之不可者也。

translations.literal: " Teng told his officers: "If I do not kill Guangsi and the others, it may be said I ruin the army's substance and lengthen the enemy's grudge—this cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: " Teng told his men, "To spare them would waste our strength and embolden the enemy—that I will not do.

sentences.zh: 公忻豎子，乃敢要人！

translations.literal: Gongxin is a stripling—how dare he make demands of men!
translations.idiomatic: This boy dares bargain with us!

sentences.zh: 」卽斬廣嗣及武，以首示之。

translations.literal: " He beheaded Guangsi and Wu at once and displayed their heads.
translations.idiomatic: " He killed Guangsi and Wu on the spot and raised their heads for all to see.

sentences.zh: 賊徒沮氣，於是出兵奮擊，盡獲之。

translations.literal: The bandits' spirit collapsed; Teng then led troops in fierce attack and captured them all.
translations.idiomatic: Morale collapsed; Teng charged and took them all.

sentences.zh: 魏恭帝三年，拜驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，轉江州刺史，爵上庸縣公，邑二千戶。

translations.literal: In the third year of Emperor Gong of Wei he was appointed General of Agile Cavalry and Grand Master of the Palace with the same honors as the Three Dukes, transferred to Inspector of Jiang Province, Duke of Shangyong with a fief of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In Wei Emperor Gong year 3 he became General of Agile Cavalry with Three-Duke honors, inspector of Jiang, and Duke of Shangyong with two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 陵州木籠獠恃險麤獷，每行抄劫，詔騰討之。

translations.literal: The Mulong Liao of Ling Province relied on the passes and were coarse and fierce, raiding whenever they marched; an edict ordered Teng to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: The Mulong Liao of Ling held the mountains, raided constantly, and Teng was sent against them.

sentences.zh: 獠旣因山為城，攻之未可拔。

translations.literal: The Liao had made the mountain their city; it could not be stormed.
translations.idiomatic: They had turned the mountain into a fortress that would not yield to assault.

sentences.zh: 騰遂於城下多設聲樂及諸雜伎，示無戰心。

translations.literal: Teng then below the city set up much music and various entertainments, showing no will to fight.
translations.idiomatic: Teng set up music and entertainers below the walls as if he had no thought of battle.

sentences.zh: 諸賊果棄其兵仗，或攜妻子臨城觀樂。

translations.literal: The bandits indeed cast aside weapons; some brought wives and children to the walls to watch the show.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders dropped their arms; some brought families to watch from the ramparts.

sentences.zh: 騰知其無備，密令衆軍俱上，諸賊惶懼，不知所為。

translations.literal: Teng knew they were unprepared and secretly ordered all armies to ascend together; the bandits were alarmed and knew not what to do.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing them off guard, he sent his men up at once; the Liao panicked.

sentences.zh: 遂縱兵討擊，盡破之，斬首一萬級，俘獲五千人。

translations.literal: He then loosed troops in pursuit and broke them completely, beheading ten thousand and capturing five thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He routed them completely—ten thousand heads and five thousand captives.

sentences.zh: 保定元年，遷隆州總管，領刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoding he was transferred to area commander of Long Province, also holding the inspectorate.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoding year 1 he became area commander of Long, retaining the inspector's seal.

sentences.zh: 二年，資州磐石民反，殺郡守，據險自守，州軍不能制。

translations.literal: In the second year the people of Panshi in Zi Province rebelled, killed the commandery administrator, held the passes, and provincial troops could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 Panshi in Zi rebelled, killed the commandery chief, and held the heights beyond provincial reach.

sentences.zh: 騰率軍討擊，盡破斬之。

translations.literal: Teng led troops to attack, broke them completely, and beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: Teng marched out, shattered them, and executed the leaders.

sentences.zh: 而蠻、獠兵及所在蜂起，山路險阻，難得掩襲。

translations.literal: Barbarian and Liao troops also rose everywhere along the roads; the mountain paths were perilous and hard to surprise.
translations.idiomatic: Tribes and Liao rose all along the routes; the trails were too steep for easy ambush.

sentences.zh: 騰遂量山川形勢，隨便開道。

translations.literal: Teng then measured mountains and rivers and opened roads wherever convenient.
translations.idiomatic: He surveyed the terrain and cut roads wherever he could.

sentences.zh: 蠻獠畏威，承風請服。

translations.literal: The barbarians and Liao feared his might and came to submit on the wind.
translations.idiomatic: Tribes submitted in waves before his authority.

sentences.zh: 所開之路，多得古銘，並是諸葛亮、桓溫舊道。

translations.literal: Among the roads he opened were many old inscriptions—all on the old routes of Zhuge Liang and Huan Wen.
translations.idiomatic: The new roads uncovered old inscriptions on routes Zhuge Liang and Huan Wen had used.

sentences.zh: 是年，鐵山獠抄斷內江路，使驛不通。

translations.literal: That year the Tieshan Liao cut the inner Jiang route and couriers could not pass.
translations.idiomatic: That year Tieshan Liao cut the inner Yangzi courier route.

sentences.zh: 騰乃進軍討之。

translations.literal: Teng then advanced to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: Teng marched to punish them.

sentences.zh: 欲至鐵山，乃偽還師。

translations.literal: Wishing to reach Tieshan, he feigned withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: To reach Tieshan he pretended to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 賊不以為虞，遂不守備。

translations.literal: The bandits did not suspect him and therefore did not guard.
translations.idiomatic: They relaxed their guard.

sentences.zh: 騰出其不意擊之，應時奔潰。

translations.literal: Teng struck them unexpectedly and they fled at once.
translations.idiomatic: He struck by surprise and they collapsed.

sentences.zh: 一日下其三城，斬其魁帥，俘獲三千人，招納降附者三萬戶。

translations.literal: In one day he took their three cities, beheaded their chiefs, captured three thousand, and received thirty thousand households in submission.
translations.idiomatic: In a single day he took three cities, killed the chiefs, took three thousand captives, and settled thirty thousand households.

sentences.zh: 帝以騰母在齊，未令東討。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Teng's mother was in Qi, did not let him campaign east.
translations.idiomatic: Because his mother was held in Qi, the emperor kept him from the eastern campaign.

sentences.zh: 適有其親屬自東還朝者，晉公護

translations.literal: It happened that a kinsman returned from the east to court; the Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu
translations.idiomatic: When a relative returned from the east, Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu

translations.literal: (Feng) [emended variant]
translations.idiomatic: [Textual note: Feng]

sentences.zh: 〔奏〕令偽告騰云：「齊為無道，已誅公家，母兄並從塗炭。

translations.literal: 〔Memorialized〕 [emended: Feng] and had him falsely tell Teng: "Qi is without the Way and has executed your clan; mother and brothers alike suffer ruin.
translations.idiomatic: memorialized a false report to Teng that Qi had executed his family and left his mother and brothers in misery.

sentences.zh: 」蓋欲發其怒也。

translations.literal: " This was meant to stir his anger.
translations.idiomatic: It was meant to enrage him.

sentences.zh: 騰乃發哀泣血，志在復讐。

translations.literal: Teng then mourned with weeping blood, his will set on revenge.
translations.idiomatic: Teng mourned until blood mingled with tears, burning for revenge.

sentences.zh: 四年，齊公憲與晉公護東征，請騰為副。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Duke of Qi Yuwen Xian and Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu campaigned east and asked that Teng serve as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 Dukes Xian and Hu marched east and asked for Teng as deputy.

sentences.zh: 趙公招時在蜀，復留之。

translations.literal: At that time Duke Zhao was in Shu and again kept him there.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Zhao was then in Shu and kept him there again.

sentences.zh: 晉公護與招書曰：「今朝廷令齊公掃蕩河、洛，欲與此人同行。

translations.literal: Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu wrote to Zhao: "The court now orders Duke of Qi to sweep He and Luo; I wish this man to go with him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Hu wrote Zhao, "The court has ordered Duke of Qi to clear He and Luo—I need this man with him.

sentences.zh: 汝彼無事，且宜借吾也。

translations.literal: You have nothing urgent there—lend him to me for now.
translations.idiomatic: You are idle there—lend him to me.

sentences.zh: 」於是命騰馳傳入朝，副憲東討。

translations.literal: " He then ordered Teng to enter court by relay post and serve Xian as deputy in the eastern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: " Teng was ordered to court by relay and joined Xian's eastern command.

sentences.zh: 五年，拜司憲中大夫。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed Director of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he became Director of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 天和初，信州蠻、蜑據江峽反叛，連結二千餘里，自稱王侯，殺刺史守令等。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianhe the barbarians and Dan of Xin Province held the river gorges in rebellion, linking more than two thousand li, calling themselves kings and marquises, and killing inspectors, administrators, and magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: At Tianhe's opening Xin tribes and Dan held the gorges for two thousand li, styled themselves kings, and killed officials.

sentences.zh: 又詔騰率軍討之。

translations.literal: An edict again ordered Teng to lead troops to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: Teng was again ordered out against them.

sentences.zh: 騰乃先趣益州，進驍勇之士，兼具樓船，沿外江而下。

translations.literal: Teng first hastened to Yi Province, advanced picked warriors, and also equipped tower ships to descend the outer river.
translations.idiomatic: He rushed to Yi, sent picked men, and floated tower ships down the outer river.

sentences.zh: 軍至湯口，分道奮擊，所向摧破。

translations.literal: When the army reached Tangkou it divided and struck fiercely; wherever it went it broke the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: At Tangkou he split his force and swept all before him.

sentences.zh: 乃築京觀以旌武功。

translations.literal: He then built a victory mound to display military achievement.
translations.idiomatic: He raised a victory mound to mark the campaign.

sentences.zh: 語在《蠻傳》。

translations.literal: The account is in the "Barbarian Treatise."
translations.idiomatic: The full account appears in the Barbarian Treatise.

sentences.zh: 涪陵郡守藺休祖又據楚、向、臨、容、開、信等州，地方二千餘里，阻兵為亂。

translations.literal: The Administrator of Fuling Commandery, Lan Xiuzu, also held Chu, Xiang, Lin, Rong, Kai, and Xin—more than two thousand li—and blocked the army in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Lan Xiuzu of Fuling also held six prefectures over two thousand li and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 復詔騰討之。

translations.literal: An edict again ordered Teng to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Teng was sent against him again.

sentences.zh: 初與大戰，斬首二千餘級，俘獲千餘人。

translations.literal: At first in great battle he beheaded more than two thousand and captured more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The first great battle cost the rebels two thousand heads and a thousand prisoners.

sentences.zh: 當時雖摧其鋒，而賊衆旣多，自夏及秋，無日不戰，師老糧盡，遂停軍集市，更思方略。

translations.literal: Though their edge was blunted, the bandit host was numerous; from summer to autumn there was fighting every day; the army grew weary and grain was exhausted, so he halted the army at Market City to rethink strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Their numbers remained vast; fighting ran daily from summer into autumn until men and grain failed, and he paused at Market City to regroup.

sentences.zh: 賊見騰不出，四面競前。

translations.literal: Seeing Teng would not come out, the bandits pressed in from all four sides.
translations.idiomatic: When he would not sally, they closed in on every side.

sentences.zh: 騰乃激勵其衆，士皆爭奮，復攻拔其魚令城，大獲糧儲，以充軍實。

translations.literal: Teng then roused his host; the men all strove eagerly; he again stormed their Yuling city, gained great stores of grain, and replenished the army.
translations.idiomatic: He roused his men to a fury, retook Yuling, and filled his granaries.

sentences.zh: 又破銅盤等七柵，前後斬獲四千人，幷船艦等。

translations.literal: He also broke seven stockades including Tongpan; in all he beheaded and captured four thousand, with ships as well.
translations.idiomatic: He broke seven stockades including Tongpan, taking four thousand heads and many ships.

sentences.zh: 又築臨州、集市二城，以鎮遏之。

translations.literal: He also built the two cities Lin Province and Market City to hold them down.
translations.idiomatic: He fortified Lin Province and Market City to hold the region.

sentences.zh: 騰自在龍州，至是前後破平諸賊，凡賞得奴婢八百口，馬牛稱是。

translations.literal: From the time Teng was in Long Province until then he had in succession broken and pacified the various bandits; in rewards he received eight hundred male and female slaves and horses and cattle in abundance.
translations.idiomatic: From his Long command onward he had crushed one rebel after another, earning eight hundred slaves and herds of livestock.

sentences.zh: 於是巴蜀悉定，詔令樹碑紀績焉。

translations.literal: Ba and Shu were then entirely settled; an edict ordered a stele erected to record his achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Ba and Shu were pacified; the court ordered a stele to record his deeds.

sentences.zh: 四年，遷江陵總管。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he was transferred to military commissioner of Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Lu Teng was made military commissioner of Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 陳遣其將章昭達率衆五萬、舩艦二千圍江陵。

translations.literal: Chen sent its general Zhang Zhaoda to lead fifty thousand men and two thousand warships to besiege Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Chen dispatched General Zhang Zhaoda with fifty thousand troops and two thousand ships to blockade Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 衛王直聞有陳寇，遣大將軍趙誾、李遷哲等率步騎赴之，並受騰節度。

translations.literal: Prince of Wei Zhi, hearing there were Chen raiders, sent Grand Generals Zhao Yin, Li Qianzhe, and others to lead infantry and cavalry to the relief, all under Teng's command.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Wei Zhi learned of the Chen incursion, he sent Grand Generals Zhao Yin and Li Qianzhe with foot and horse to reinforce the city, all under Lu Teng's orders.

sentences.zh: 時遷哲等守外城，陳將程文季、雷道勤夜來掩襲，遷哲等驚亂，不能抗禦。

translations.literal: At the time Qianzhe and the others held the outer city; Chen generals Cheng Wenji and Lei Daoqin came by night in a surprise attack; Qianzhe and the others were thrown into disorder and could not resist.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qianzhe held the outer walls when Chen generals Cheng Wenji and Lei Daoqin struck by night; his men panicked and could not hold.

sentences.zh: 騰夜遣開門，出甲士奮擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Teng by night ordered the gates opened, sent out armored soldiers in fierce assault, and routed them greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Teng opened the gates by night, sent armored troops out in a fierce charge, and broke them completely.

sentences.zh: 陳人奔潰，道勤中流矢而斃，虜獲二百餘人。

translations.literal: Chen men fled in collapse; Daoqin was hit by a flying arrow and died; more than two hundred were captured.
translations.idiomatic: The Chen force scattered; Lei Daoqin took an arrow and died; more than two hundred were taken.

sentences.zh: 陳人又決龍川寧邦堤，引水灌江陵城。

translations.literal: Chen men also breached the Longchuan Ningbang dike, drawing water to flood Jiangling city.
translations.idiomatic: The Chen army also broke the Longchuan Ningbang dike and diverted water to flood Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 騰親率將士戰於西堤，破之，斬首數千級，陳人乃遁。

translations.literal: Teng personally led officers and soldiers to fight at the western dike, broke them, beheaded several thousand, and the Chen men then fled.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Teng led his troops in person at the western dike, routed the enemy, took several thousand heads, and the Chen withdrew.

sentences.zh: 六年，進位柱國，進爵上庸郡公，增邑通前三千五百戶。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he was advanced to pillar-of-state, raised to Duke of Shangyong commandery, fief increased with prior holdings to three thousand five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was made pillar-of-state and Duke of Shangyong, his fief rising with earlier grants to thirty-five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 建德二年，徵拜大司空，尋出為涇州總管。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiande, he was summoned and appointed Grand Minister of Works; soon sent out as military commissioner of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiande year 2 he was recalled as Grand Minister of Works, then posted out as military commissioner of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 宣政元年冬，薨於京師。

translations.literal: In the winter of the first year of Xuanzheng, he died at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Xuanzheng year 1 he died at the capital.

sentences.zh: 贈本官加幷汾等五州刺史，重贈大後丞。

translations.literal: Granted his former office plus Inspector of five prefectures including Bing and Fen; again posthumously granted Grand Rear Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously given his former rank plus inspector of five prefectures including Bing and Fen, and again honored as Grand Rear Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 諡曰定。

translations.literal: Posthumous title Ding.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous name was Ding (Settled).

sentences.zh: 子玄嗣。

translations.literal: His son Xuan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xuan succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 玄字士鑒，騰入關時，年始七歲。

translations.literal: Xuan, styled Shijian; when Teng entered the Passes, he was just seven.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan, styled Shijian, was only seven when Lu Teng entered the Passes.

sentences.zh: 仕齊為奉朝請，歷成平縣令。

translations.literal: He served Qi as Court Gentleman for Court Assembly and passed through as magistrate of Chengping county.
translations.idiomatic: Under Northern Qi he served as court gentleman for court assembly and later as magistrate of Chengping county.

sentences.zh: 齊平，高祖見玄，特加勞勉，卽拜地官府都上士。

translations.literal: When Qi was pacified, Gaozu saw Xuan and especially added encouragement and comfort, immediately appointing him Chief Clerk of the Earth Office Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: After Qi fell, Emperor Gaozu received Xuan with special praise and at once made him chief clerk of the Earth Office Bureau.

sentences.zh: 大象末，為隋文相府內兵參軍。

translations.literal: At the end of Daxiang, he became Internal Military Adjutant in Yang Jian's chancellor's office.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Daxiang reign he became internal military adjutant in Yang Jian's chancellor's office.

sentences.zh: 玄弟融，字士傾，最知名，少歷顯職。

translations.literal: Xuan's younger brother Rong, styled Shiqing, was the most renowned; in youth he passed through distinguished offices.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan's younger brother Rong, styled Shiqing, was the better known of the two and in youth held a series of high posts.

sentences.zh: 大象中，位至大將軍、定陵縣公。

translations.literal: In Daxiang, he reached Grand General and Duke of Dingling county.
translations.idiomatic: Under Daxiang he rose to grand general and Duke of Dingling county.

sentences.zh: 賀若敦，代人也。

translations.literal: He Ruodun was a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: He Ruodun came from Dai.

sentences.zh: 父統，為東魏潁州長史。

translations.literal: His father Tong served Eastern Wei as chief clerk of Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tong had been chief clerk of Ying Province under Eastern Wei.

sentences.zh: 大統

translations.literal: Great Unity
translations.idiomatic: In the Great Unity era

translations.literal: (two) [emended variant]
translations.idiomatic: year two

sentences.zh: 年，執刺史田迅以州降。

translations.literal: year, he seized Prefect Tian Xun and surrendered the province.
translations.idiomatic: he seized Prefect Tian Xun and surrendered the province.

sentences.zh: 至長安，魏文帝謂統曰：「卿自潁川從我，何日能忘。

translations.literal: Reaching Chang'an, Emperor Wen of Wei said to Tong: "You followed me from Yingchuan—what day could I forget?
translations.idiomatic: At Chang'an Emperor Wen of Wei told Tong, "You came with me from Yingchuan—when could I forget that?

sentences.zh: 」卽拜右衛將軍、散騎常侍、兗州刺史，賜爵當亭縣公。

translations.literal: " He was immediately appointed Right Guard General, Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary, Inspector of Yan Province, and enfeoffed Duke of Dangting county.
translations.idiomatic: " Tong was at once made Right Guard General, regular attendant-in-ordinary, and inspector of Yan, and enfeoffed as Duke of Dangting county.

sentences.zh: 尋除北雍州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon removed and made Inspector of Northern Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to inspector of Northern Yong.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈侍中、燕朔恆三州刺史、司空公，諡曰哀。

translations.literal: On death, posthumously granted Attendant-in-Ordinary, Inspector of Yan, Shuo, and Heng Provinces, Duke of Works, posthumous title Ai.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously honored as attendant-in-ordinary, inspector of Yan, Shuo, and Heng, and Duke of Works, with the posthumous name Ai (Lamented).

sentences.zh: 敦少有氣幹，善騎射。

translations.literal: Dun from youth had spirit and capacity; skilled at mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: He Ruodun as a youth had force of character and was expert with bow and horse.

sentences.zh: 統之謀執迅也，慮事不果，又以累弱旣多，難以自拔，沉吟者久之。

translations.literal: In Tong's plot to seize Xun, he feared the affair would not succeed, and also because dependents were many and escape would be hard; he brooded a long time.
translations.idiomatic: When Tong planned to seize Tian Xun, he worried the scheme might fail and that with so many dependents withdrawal would be hard; he hesitated for a long while.

sentences.zh: 敦時年十七，乃進策曰：「大人往事葛榮，已為將帥；

translations.literal: Dun was then seventeen; he advanced a plan, saying: "Father, you formerly served Ge Rong and were already general and commander;
translations.idiomatic: He Ruodun was seventeen. He offered counsel: "Father, you once served Ge Rong as a field commander;

sentences.zh: 後入爾朱，禮遇猶重。

translations.literal: later you entered the Erzhu clan's service, and the courtesy and treatment were still heavy.
translations.idiomatic: later you entered Erzhu service and were still treated with great honor.

sentences.zh: 韓陵之役，屈節高歡，旣非故人，又無功效，今日委任，無異於前者，正以天下未定，方藉英雄之力。

translations.literal: At the battle of Hanling you submitted to Gao Huan; he was neither an old friend nor had you merit; today's commission is no different from the former—only because the realm is not settled and they rely on heroes' strength for the moment.
translations.idiomatic: At Hanling you bowed to Gao Huan—no old tie, no fresh merit—yet today's appointment is the same as before, only because the realm is unsettled and men of force are still needed.

sentences.zh: 一旦清平，豈有相容之理。

translations.literal: Once peace is restored, there can be no principle of mutual accommodation.
translations.idiomatic: Once the world is at peace, they will not suffer you to remain.

sentences.zh: 以敦愚計，恐將來有危亡之憂。

translations.literal: By Dun's foolish reckoning, I fear there will be peril and ruin hereafter.
translations.idiomatic: By my poor reckoning, ruin lies ahead.

sentences.zh: 願思全身遠害，不得有所顧念也。

translations.literal: I wish you would consider preserving body and keeping afar from harm—you must not hold any lingering attachment.
translations.idiomatic: Think of saving yourself and keeping clear of harm—do not let affection hold you back.

sentences.zh: 」統乃流涕從之，遂定謀歸太祖。

translations.literal: " Tong then wept and followed it, and thus fixed the plan to submit to Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: " Tong wept and agreed, and they settled on submitting to Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai.

sentences.zh: 時羣盜蜂起，各據山谷。

translations.literal: At the time bandits rose everywhere like bees, each holding mountain valleys.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits were swarming then, each band holding its own hills.

sentences.zh: 大龜山賊張世顯潛來襲統，敦挺身赴戰，手斬七八人，賊乃退走。

translations.literal: Bandits of Great Turtle Mountain, Zhang Shixian, secretly came to raid Tong; Dun threw himself forward into battle, personally beheading seven or eight men, and the bandits then retreated.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shixian of Great Turtle Mountain secretly attacked Tong; He Ruodun rushed into the fight, killed seven or eight men himself, and drove the bandits off.

sentences.zh: 統大悅，謂左右僚屬曰：「我少從軍旅，戰陣非一，如此兒年時膽略者，未見其人。

translations.literal: Tong was greatly pleased and said to his attendant officials: "I have followed the army from youth; battle lines have not been few—such courage and strategy at this lad's age, I have never seen his like.
translations.idiomatic: Tong was delighted and told his staff, "I have soldiered since youth and seen many battles, yet never a boy of such nerve and wit.

sentences.zh: 非唯成我門戶，亦當為國名將。」

translations.literal: Not only will he establish our house; he will also become a famed general of the state."
translations.idiomatic: He will not only honor our house—he will be a famous general of the realm."

sentences.zh: 明年，從河內〔公〕獨孤信於洛陽，被圍。

translations.literal: Next year, following Henan 〔Gong〕 [emended: Duke of Henan] Dugu Xin at Luoyang, besieged.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he followed Dugu Xin, Duke of Henan, to Luoyang and was caught in the siege.

sentences.zh: 敦彎弓三石，箭不虛發。

translations.literal: Dun bent a three-stone bow; arrows never missed.
translations.idiomatic: He Ruodun drew a three-stone bow and never wasted a shot.

sentences.zh: 信大奇之，乃言於太祖。

translations.literal: Xin was greatly astonished and spoke of it to Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: Dugu Xin was astonished and reported it to Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai.

sentences.zh: 太祖異之，引置麾下，授都督，封安陵縣伯，邑四百戶。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor was struck by it, took him under his command, granted him area commander, enfeoffed Baron of Anling county with four hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai took him into his own command, made him area commander, and enfeoffed him Baron of Anling with four hundred households.

sentences.zh: 嘗從太祖校獵於甘泉宮，時圍人不齊，獸多逃逸，太祖大怒，人皆股戰。

translations.literal: Once he followed Grand Progenitor in a hunting exercise at Ganquan Palace; at the time the beaters were not complete, many beasts escaped, Grand Progenitor was greatly angry, all men trembled at the thighs.
translations.idiomatic: Once at Ganquan Palace he joined Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai on a hunt; the beat was incomplete, game broke out everywhere, and the Grand Progenitor's rage made every man shake.

sentences.zh: 圍內唯有一鹿，俄亦突圍而走。

translations.literal: Within the beat there was only one deer; soon it too broke the ring and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Only one deer remained inside the ring, and it too broke out and ran.

sentences.zh: 敦躍馬馳之，鹿上東山，敦棄馬步逐至山半，便掣之而下。

translations.literal: Dun leapt on horse and galloped after it; the deer went up Eastern Mountain; Dun abandoned horse and pursued on foot to halfway up the hill, then seized it and brought it down.
translations.idiomatic: He Ruodun spurred after it up Eastern Mountain, left his horse, ran it down on foot halfway up the slope, seized it, and brought it back.

sentences.zh: 太祖大悅，諸將因得免責。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor was greatly pleased; the generals thereby escaped blame.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai was delighted, and the other officers were spared his wrath.

sentences.zh: 累遷太子庶子、撫軍將軍、通直散騎常侍、大都督、車騎大將軍、散騎常侍、儀同三司，進爵廣鄉縣侯。

translations.literal: Repeatedly promoted: Companion of the Heir Apparent, General Who Pacifies the Army, Regular Attendant of Unimpeded Access, Grand Area Commander, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary, Equal-in-Honor to the Three Divisions, advanced in rank to Marquis of Guangxiang county.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through Companion of the Heir Apparent, General Who Pacifies the Army, regular attendant of unimpeded access, grand area commander, grand general of chariots and cavalry, regular attendant-in-ordinary, and equal-in-honor to the three divisions, and was advanced to Marquis of Guangxiang.

sentences.zh: 敦旣有武藝，太祖恆欲以將帥任之。

translations.literal: Dun having martial skill, Grand Progenitor always wished to assign him as general and commander.
translations.idiomatic: Because He Ruodun had martial talent, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai always meant to give him command.

sentences.zh: 魏廢帝二年，拜右衛將軍，俄加驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，進爵為公。

translations.literal: In the second year of Deposed Emperor of Wei, appointed Right Guard General; soon added Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Opening Grandee Equal in Honor to the Three Divisions, advanced in rank to duke.
translations.idiomatic: In Deposed Emperor year 2 he became Right Guard General, soon grand general of agile cavalry and opening grandee equal in honor to the three divisions, and was raised to duke.

sentences.zh: 時岷蜀初開，民情尚梗。

translations.literal: At the time Min and Shu had newly been opened; the people's hearts were still resistant.
translations.idiomatic: Min and Shu had only lately been opened, and the people were still restive.

sentences.zh: 巴西人譙淹據南梁州，與梁西江州刺史王開業共為表裏，扇動群蠻。

translations.literal: Qiao Yan of Ba commandery held Southern Liang Province, with Liang's Inspector of Western Jiang Province Wang Kaiye as mutual support inside and out, inciting the various Man.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Yan of Ba held Southern Liang and coordinated with Liang inspector of Western Jiang Wang Kaiye, inside and out, to stir up the tribal chiefs.

sentences.zh: 太祖令敦率軍討之。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor ordered Dun to lead an army to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai ordered He Ruodun to lead troops against him.

sentences.zh: 山路艱險，人跡罕至。

translations.literal: Mountain roads were steep and dangerous; human tracks rarely reached.
translations.idiomatic: The mountain paths were steep and barely passable.

sentences.zh: 敦身先將士，攀木緣崖，倍道兼行，乘其不意。

translations.literal: Dun went ahead of officers and soldiers, climbing trees and scaling cliffs, advancing by double marches, striking while they were unexpecting.
translations.idiomatic: He Ruodun led from the front, climbing trees and cliffs, forcing double marches, and struck before the enemy knew he was there.

sentences.zh: 又遣儀同扶猛破其別帥向鎮侯於白帝。

translations.literal: He also sent Equal-in-Honor Fu Meng to break their separate commander Xiang Zhenhou at White Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Fu Meng, equal in honor to the three divisions, to defeat their sub-commander Xiang Zhenhou at White Emperor.

sentences.zh: 淹乃與開業幷其黨泉玉成、侯造等率衆七千，口累三萬，自墊江而下，就梁王琳。

translations.literal: Yan then with Kaiye together with his partisans Quan Yucheng, Hou Zao, and others led seven thousand men, dependents numbering thirty thousand, from Dianjiang downstream, joining Liang's Prince Wang Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Yan then joined Wang Kaiye and his allies Quan Yucheng and Hou Zao with seven thousand fighting men and thirty thousand dependents, sailing down from Dianjiang to Wang Lin of Liang.

sentences.zh: 敦邀擊，破之。

translations.literal: Dun intercepted and struck, broke them.
translations.idiomatic: He Ruodun intercepted and routed them.

sentences.zh: 淹復依山立柵，南引蠻帥向白彪為援。

translations.literal: Yan again relied on the mountains to set palisades, southward drawing Man commander Xiang Baibiao as support.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Yan fortified the hills again and called in the Man chief Xiang Baibiao from the south as reinforcement.

sentences.zh: 敦設反間，離其黨與，因其懈怠，復破之。

translations.literal: Dun set counter-intelligence, separated his partisans, and while they were lax again broke them.
translations.idiomatic: He Ruodun sowed discord among their allies and, catching them off guard, broke them again.

sentences.zh: 斬淹，盡俘其衆。

translations.literal: Beheaded Yan; captured all his masses.
translations.idiomatic: He beheaded Qiao Yan and took all his followers captive.

sentences.zh: 進爵武都公，增邑通前一千七百戶，拜典祀中大夫。

translations.literal: Advanced in rank to Duke of Wudu, fief increased with prior to one thousand seven hundred households; appointed Director of Ceremonies Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to Duke of Wudu, his fief rising with earlier grants to seventeen hundred households, and made director of ceremonies grandee.

sentences.zh: 尋出為金州都督、七州諸軍事、金州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon sent out as Area Commander of Jin, military affairs of seven provinces, Inspector of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon posted as area commander of Jin, commander-in-chief of military affairs in seven provinces, and inspector of Jin.

sentences.zh: 向白彪又與蠻帥向五子等聚衆為寇，圍逼信州。

translations.literal: Xiang Baibiao again with Man commander Xiang Wuzi and others gathered masses as raiders, besieging and pressing Xin Province.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Baibiao joined the Man chief Xiang Wuzi and others in raiding and pressing Xin Province.

sentences.zh: 詔敦與開府田弘赴救，未至而城已陷。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Dun and Opening Grandee Tian Hong to go to the rescue; before they arrived the city had already fallen.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent He Ruodun and opening grandee Tian Hong to relieve the city, but it had already fallen before they arrived.

sentences.zh: 進與白彪等戰，破之，俘斬二千人。

translations.literal: Advancing to battle with Baibiao and others, broke them, captured and beheaded two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced against Baibiao and the rest, defeated them, and killed or captured two thousand.

sentences.zh: 仍進軍追討，遂平信州。

translations.literal: Still advancing the army in pursuit, thus pacified Xin Province.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing the pursuit, he pacified Xin Province.

sentences.zh: 是歲，荊州蠻帥文子榮自號仁州刺史，擁逼土人，據沮漳為逆。

translations.literal: That year, Jing Province Man commander Wen Zirong styled himself Inspector of Ren Province, coercing the native people, holding the Ju and Zhang rivers in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Jing Man chief Wen Zirong styled himself inspector of Ren, coerced the locals, and rebelled along the Ju and Zhang rivers.

sentences.zh: 復令敦與開府潘招討之，擒子榮，幷虜其衆。

translations.literal: Again ordered Dun with Opening Grandee Pan to campaign and strike; captured Zirong together with his masses.
translations.idiomatic: He Ruodun was again ordered out with opening grandee Pan to suppress them; he captured Wen Zirong and his followers.

sentences.zh: 初，土人亟乘輕船，載米粟及籠雞鴨以餉瑱軍。

translations.literal: Earlier, native people frequently took light boats, loading grain and millet and caged chickens and ducks to supply Wang Lin's army.
translations.idiomatic: Until then locals had often poled light boats laden with grain and caged fowl to Wang Lin's camp.

sentences.zh: 敦患之，乃偽為土人，裝船伏甲士於中。

translations.literal: Dun was troubled by this; he feigned being native people, fitted out boats, and hid armored men within.
translations.idiomatic: He Ruodun countered by fitting out boats like local supply craft and hiding armored men inside.

sentences.zh: 瑱兵人望見，謂餉船之至，逆來爭取。

translations.literal: Wang Lin's soldiers saw from afar, thinking supply boats had arrived, came to meet and competed to seize.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lin's men sighted them from afar, thought provisions had arrived, and rushed out to seize the boats.

sentences.zh: 敦甲士出而擒之。

translations.literal: Dun's armored men came out and captured them.
translations.idiomatic: He Ruodun's soldiers burst out and took them captive.

sentences.zh: 敦軍數有叛人乘馬投瑱者，輒納之。

translations.literal: Dun's army repeatedly had deserters who rode horses to defect to Wang Lin; Lin always accepted them.
translations.idiomatic: Many of He Ruodun's men kept deserting on horseback to Wang Lin, and Wang Lin took them in.

sentences.zh: 敦又別取一馬，牽以趣船，令船中逆以鞭鞭之。

translations.literal: Dun also separately took a horse, led it toward the boats, had men in the boats from below whip it with whips.
translations.idiomatic: He Ruodun also took another horse, led it to a boat, and had sailors below whip it from underneath.

sentences.zh: 如是者再三，馬便畏船不上。

translations.literal: Thus several times; the horse then feared boats and would not board.
translations.idiomatic: He did this again and again until the horse feared boats and would not board.

sentences.zh: 後伏兵於江岸，遣人以招瑱軍，詐稱投附。

translations.literal: Later he hid troops on the riverbank, sent men to entice Wang Lin's army, falsely claiming defection.
translations.idiomatic: Then he hid troops on the bank and sent men on the frightened horse to lure Wang Lin's army, pretending to defect.

sentences.zh: 瑱便遣兵迎接，競來牽馬。

translations.literal: Wang Lin then sent troops to welcome; they vied to seize the horse.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lin sent men to welcome the rider, and they crowded forward to seize the horse.

sentences.zh: 馬旣畏船不上，敦發伏掩之，盡殪。

translations.literal: The horse already fearing boats would not board; Dun's ambush sprang forth and slaughtered them all.
translations.idiomatic: The horse would not board; the ambush rose and slaughtered them all.

sentences.zh: 此後實有饋餉及亡命奔瑱者，猶謂敦之設詐，逆遣扞擊，並不敢受。

translations.literal: After this there were real supply deliveries and fugitives who fled to Wang Lin, yet they still thought it Dun's stratagem, sent out to repulse and strike, and none dared accept.
translations.idiomatic: After that, even real supplies and real deserters Wang Lin treated as tricks and drove away.

sentences.zh: 相持歲餘，瑱等不能制，求借船送敦度江。

translations.literal: Facing each other more than a year, Wang Lin and others could not control him, asked to borrow boats to send Dun across the river.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year facing each other without advantage, Wang Lin asked to lend boats to ferry He Ruodun across the river.

sentences.zh: 敦慮其或詐，拒而弗許。

translations.literal: Dun feared they might deceive, refused and did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: He Ruodun suspected a trap and refused.

sentences.zh: 瑱復遣使謂敦曰：「驃騎在此旣久，今欲給船相送，何為不去？

translations.literal: Wang Lin again sent an envoy saying to Dun: "The Grand General of Agile Cavalry has been here long; now I wish to provide boats to send you across—why do you not go?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lin sent another envoy: "You have been here long enough; I mean to give you boats to cross—why will you not go?

sentences.zh: 」敦報云：「湘州是我國家之地，為爾侵逼。

translations.literal: " Dun replied: "Xiang Province is our state's land—you encroached upon it.
translations.idiomatic: " He Ruodun answered: "Xiang Province belongs to our state—you invaded it.

sentences.zh: 敦來之日，欲相平殄。

translations.literal: The day Dun came, he wished to level and destroy you.
translations.idiomatic: I came to destroy you.

sentences.zh: 旣未得一決，所以不去。
