translations.literal: Since we have not yet had one decisive settlement, that is why I do not leave."
translations.idiomatic: We have not yet fought it out—that is why I stay."

sentences.zh: 」瑱後日復遣使來，敦謂使者云：「必須我還，可舍我百里，當為汝去。

translations.literal: Wang Lin again on another day sent an envoy; Dun told the envoy: "If you must have me return, withdraw a hundred li from me, and I will go for you."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lin sent an envoy again; He Ruodun told him: "If you want me gone, pull back a hundred li and I will leave."

sentences.zh: 」瑱等留船於江，將兵去津路百里。

translations.literal: Wang Lin and others left boats on the river, led troops away from the ford road a hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lin left boats on the river and withdrew his troops a hundred li from the crossing.

sentences.zh: 敦覘知非詐，徐理舟烜，勒衆而還。

translations.literal: Dun observed and knew it was not deceit; slowly put the boats in order, marshaled the host and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing no trick, He Ruodun slowly made ready the boats, mustered his force, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 在軍病死者十五六。

translations.literal: In the army fifteen or sixteen of every hundred died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen or sixteen men in every hundred in the army died of sickness.

sentences.zh: 晉公護以敦失地無功，除名為民。

translations.literal: Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu, because Dun lost territory without achievement, removed his name and made him a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu, finding that He Ruodun had lost ground without merit, struck his name from the rolls and reduced him to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 保定二年，拜工部中大夫。

translations.literal: In the second year of Baoding, appointed Grandee of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoding year 2 he was appointed grandee of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 尋出為金州總管、七州諸軍事、金州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon sent out as military commissioner of Jin, military affairs of seven provinces, Inspector of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon posted out as military commissioner of Jin, commander-in-chief of military affairs in seven provinces, and inspector of Jin.

sentences.zh: 三年，從柱國楊忠引突厥破齊長城，至幷州而還，以敦為殿。

translations.literal: In the third year, following Pillar-of-State Yang Zhong he led the Türks to break Northern Qi's Great Wall, reaching Bing Province and returning; Dun was rear guard.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he followed pillar-of-state Yang Zhong with the Türks to breach Northern Qi's Great Wall, reaching Bing Province on the return; He Ruodun commanded the rear guard.

sentences.zh: 別封一子順義縣公，邑一千戶。

translations.literal: Separately enfeoffed one son as Duke of Shunyi county, fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: One son was separately enfeoffed Duke of Shunyi county with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 五年，除中州刺史，鎮函谷。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, removed and made Inspector of Central Province, garrisoning Hangu Pass.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he was made inspector of Central Province and posted to garrison Hangu Pass.

sentences.zh: 敦恃功負氣，顧其流輩皆為大將軍，敦獨未得，兼以湘州之役，全軍而反，不蒙旌賞，翻被除名，每懷怨怒。

translations.literal: Dun relied on merit and bore himself proudly; looking back, his peers had all become grand generals while Dun alone had not yet received it; moreover, in the Xiang Province campaign he returned with the whole army yet received no commendation or reward, instead being struck from the rolls—he constantly harbored resentment and anger.
translations.idiomatic: He Ruodun, proud of his record, saw men of his generation made grand generals while he alone had not; the Xiangzhou campaign had ended with his army intact, yet he won no reward and was disgraced instead—he nursed grievance and rage.

sentences.zh: 屬有臺使至，乃出怨言。

translations.literal: When a commissioner from the headquarters arrived, he then voiced complaints.
translations.idiomatic: When an envoy from the commissionerate arrived, Dun began airing grievances.

sentences.zh: 晉公護怒，遂徵敦還，逼令自殺。

translations.literal: Duke of Jin Hu was enraged, and thereupon summoned Dun back and forced him to kill himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Hu, Duke of Jin, flew into a rage, recalled Dun, and compelled him to commit suicide.

sentences.zh: 時年四十九。

translations.literal: His age was then forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He was forty-nine at the time.

sentences.zh: 建德初，追贈大將軍。

translations.literal: At the start of Jiande, posthumously honored as Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: In the opening year of Jiande he was posthumously made grand general.

sentences.zh: 諡曰烈。

translations.literal: Posthumous title: Lie.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously named Lie.

sentences.zh: 子弼，有文武材略。

translations.literal: His son Bi had both civil and military talent and stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bi possessed civil and military ability in equal measure.

sentences.zh: 大象末，位至開府儀同大將軍、揚州刺史、襄邑縣公。

translations.literal: At the end of Daxiang, he reached Opening-establishment, General Honor Equal to the Three Excellencies, Inspector of Yang Province, and Duke of Xiangyi County.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of Daxiang he had risen to opening-establishment general, honor equal to the three excellencies, inspector of Yang Province, and duke of Xiangyi county.

sentences.zh: 敦弟誼，亦知名。

translations.literal: Dun's younger brother Yi was also well known.
translations.idiomatic: Dun's younger brother Yi won fame as well.

sentences.zh: 官至柱國、海陵縣公。

translations.literal: He reached the post of Pillar-of-State and Duke of Hailing County.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to pillar-of-state and duke of Hailing county.

sentences.zh: 權景宣字暉遠，天水顯親人也。

translations.literal: Quan Jingxuan, styled Huiyuan, was a man of Xianqin in Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Jingxuan, styled Huiyuan, came from Xianqin in Tianshui commandery.

sentences.zh: 父曇騰，魏隴西郡守。

translations.literal: His father Tanteng was Wei prefect of Longxi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tanteng had served Wei as prefect of Longxi commandery.

sentences.zh: 贈秦州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously honored as Inspector of Qin Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made inspector of Qin Province.

sentences.zh: 景宣少聰悟，有氣俠，宗黨皆歎異之。

translations.literal: Jingxuan in youth was sharp and perceptive, possessed spirit and chivalry, and kinsmen all sighed in wonder at him.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Jingxuan was quick-witted and bold-hearted; his clan marveled at him.

sentences.zh: 年十七，魏行臺蕭寶夤見而奇之，表為輕車將軍。

translations.literal: At age seventeen, Wei Grand Commissioner Xiao Baoyin saw him and considered him extraordinary, and memorialized him as General of Light Chariots.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen the Wei grand commissioner Xiao Baoyin took notice of him and recommended him as general of light chariots.

sentences.zh: 及寶夤敗，景宣歸鄉里。

translations.literal: When Baoyin was defeated, Jingxuan returned to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: After Baoyin's defeat Jingxuan went home to his native place.

sentences.zh: 太祖平隴右，擢為行臺郎中。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor pacified Longyou, he was promoted to Bureau Director of the Grand Commissionerate.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai pacified Longyou, Jingxuan was raised to bureau director of the grand commissionerate.

sentences.zh: 魏孝武西遷，授鎮遠將軍、步兵校尉，加平西將軍、秦州大中正。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, he was appointed General Who Pacifies the Distances and Commandant of Foot Soldiers, with the added titles General Who Pacifies the West and Grand Rectifier of Qin Province.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, he received the posts of general who pacifies the distances and commandant of foot soldiers, with the added rank of general who pacifies the west and grand rectifier of Qin Province.

sentences.zh: 大統初，轉祠部郎中。

translations.literal: At the start of Datong, transferred to Bureau Director of Sacrificial Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Datong he was transferred to bureau director of sacrificial affairs.

sentences.zh: 景宣曉兵權，有智略。

translations.literal: Jingxuan understood military authority and had wisdom and stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan grasped the art of command and was shrewd in counsel.

sentences.zh: 從太祖拔弘農，破沙苑，皆先登陷陣。

translations.literal: Following the Grand Progenitor he took Hongnong and broke Shiyuan; in each he was first to ascend and break the enemy ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning under Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai, he helped capture Hongnong and win at Shiyuan, always in the van when the lines closed.

sentences.zh: 轉外兵郎中。

translations.literal: Transferred to Bureau Director of External Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to bureau director of external military affairs.

sentences.zh: 從開府于謹援洛陽，景宣督課糧儲，軍以周濟。

translations.literal: Following Opening-establishment Yu Jin to relieve Luoyang, Jingxuan supervised provisioning of grain stores, and the army was fully supplied.
translations.idiomatic: When he followed Yu Jin, holder of an opening establishment, to relieve Luoyang, Jingxuan organized grain stores and kept the army fed.

sentences.zh: 時初復洛陽，將修繕宮室，景宣率徒三千，先出采運。

translations.literal: At the time Luoyang had just been recovered and palace halls were to be repaired; Jingxuan led three thousand laborers and went out first to gather and transport materials.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang had only just been retaken and the palaces were to be rebuilt; Jingxuan took three thousand workers ahead to fetch timber and supplies.

sentences.zh: 會東魏兵至，司州牧元季海等以衆少拔還，屬城悉叛，道路擁塞。

translations.literal: When Eastern Wei troops arrived, Inspector of Si Province Yuan Jihai and others withdrew for having too few men; dependent cities all rebelled, and the roads were choked.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei forces then appeared; Yuan Jihai, inspector of Si Province, and others pulled back with too small a force, every subordinate city turned, and the roads jammed with refugees.

sentences.zh: 景宣將二十騎，且戰且走。

translations.literal: Jingxuan had twenty horsemen; they fought as they fled.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan rode with twenty men, fighting a running retreat.

sentences.zh: 從騎略盡，景宣輕馬突圍，手斬數級，馳而獲免，因投民家自匿。

translations.literal: His followers were nearly all gone; Jingxuan on a light horse burst through the encirclement, personally beheaded several enemies, galloped to safety, and took refuge hiding in a commoner's home.
translations.idiomatic: When his escort was almost wiped out, he broke out on a swift horse, killed several foes with his own hand, rode clear, and hid in a farmer's house.

sentences.zh: 景宣以久藏非計，乃偽作太祖書，招募得五百餘人，保據宜陽，聲言大軍續至。

translations.literal: Jingxuan thought long hiding was no plan; he forged a letter in the Grand Progenitor's name, recruited more than five hundred men, held Yiyang, and declared that the main army would soon arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing he could not stay hidden forever, he forged orders from Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai, raised five hundred-odd men, seized Yiyang, and spread word that a great host was on its way.

sentences.zh: 東魏將段琛等率衆至九曲，憚景宣，不敢進。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei general Duan Chen and others led troops to Jiuqu; they feared Jingxuan and dared not advance.
translations.idiomatic: When Eastern Wei generals led by Duan Chen reached Jiuqu, they were wary of Jingxuan and held back.

sentences.zh: 景宣恐琛審其虛實，乃將腹心自隨，詐云迎軍，因得西遁。

translations.literal: Jingxuan feared Chen would probe his strength; taking trusted men with him he feigned going to welcome the army and thus escaped west.
translations.idiomatic: Afraid Chen would test his bluff, he took a few trusted followers, pretended he was going to meet the relief force, and slipped away westward.

sentences.zh: 與儀同李延孫相會，攻孔城。

translations.literal: He joined Honor Equal to the Three Excellencies Li Yansun and attacked Kongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He linked up with Li Yansun, honor equal to the three excellencies, and stormed Kongcheng.

sentences.zh: 洛陽以南，尋亦來附。

translations.literal: South of Luoyang, districts soon also came over.
translations.idiomatic: Territory south of Luoyang soon submitted as well.

sentences.zh: 太祖卽留景宣守張白塢，節度東南義軍。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor then left Jingxuan to hold Zhangbaiwu and to direct the righteous armies of the southeast.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai then posted Jingxuan at Zhangbaiwu to command the loyalist forces of the southeast.

sentences.zh: 東魏將王元

translations.literal: Eastern Wei general Wang Yuan
translations.idiomatic: An Eastern Wei commander of the Wang clan

translations.literal: (Kai) [emended variant].
translations.idiomatic: [Textual variant: Kai]

sentences.zh: 〔軌〕入洛，景宣與延孫等擊走之，以功授大行臺右丞。

translations.literal: 〔Gui〕 [emended: Kai] entered Luoyang; Jingxuan with Yan Sun and others drove them off, and for merit was appointed Right Director of the Grand Commissionerate.
translations.idiomatic: When Eastern Wei general Wang Yuan Gui entered Luoyang, Jingxuan and Li Yansun beat him back, and Jingxuan was rewarded as right director of the grand commissionerate.

sentences.zh: 進屯宜陽，攻襄城，拔之，獲郡守王洪顯，俘斬五百餘人。

translations.literal: He advanced and encamped at Yiyang, attacked Xiangcheng, took it, captured the commandery prefect Wang Hongxian, and captured or beheaded more than five hundred.
translations.idiomatic: He moved on Yiyang, stormed Xiangcheng, seized the prefect Wang Hongxian, and killed or captured more than five hundred men.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘉之，徵入朝。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor praised this and summoned him to court.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai commended him and called him to court.

sentences.zh: 錄前後功，封顯親縣男，邑三百戶。

translations.literal: His past and present achievements were recorded; he was enfeoffed as Baron of Xianqin County with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: His services were tallied and he was enfeoffed baron of Xianqin county with three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 除南陽郡守。

translations.literal: Appointed administrator of Nanyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was made administrator of Nanyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 郡鄰敵境，舊制，發民守防三十五處，多廢農桑，而姦宄猶作。

translations.literal: The commandery bordered enemy territory; under the old system, the people were mobilized to guard thirty-five posts, farming and sericulture were much neglected, yet bandits still acted.
translations.idiomatic: Nanyang lay on the frontier; by old custom the people were posted at thirty-five defense points, fields went untilled, and robbers still flourished.

sentences.zh: 景宣至，並除之，唯修起城樓，多備器械，寇盜斂跡，民得肄業。

translations.literal: When Jingxuan arrived, he abolished all of this; he only repaired tower-gates, stocked many weapons, bandits and robbers withdrew, and the people could return to cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan ended the practice, rebuilt the gate towers, piled up arms, and the countryside grew quiet enough for farming to resume.

sentences.zh: 百姓稱之，立碑頌德。

translations.literal: The common people praised him and erected a stele extolling his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The people praised him and raised a stele to his merit.

sentences.zh: 太祖特賞粟帛，以旌其能。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor specially rewarded him with grain and silk to honor his ability.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai sent grain and silk as a special reward for his competence.

sentences.zh: 遷廣州刺史。

translations.literal: Transferred to Inspector of Guang Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to inspector of Guang Province.

sentences.zh: 侯景舉河南來附，景宣從僕射王思政經略應接。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing offered Henan in submission, Jingxuan followed Vice Director Wang Sizheng in strategy to receive him.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing surrendered Henan, Jingxuan worked under Vice Director Wang Sizheng to manage the handover.

sentences.zh: 旣而侯景南叛，恐東魏復有其地，以景宣為大都督、豫州刺史，鎮樂口。

translations.literal: Before long Hou Jing rebelled southward; fearing Eastern Wei would recover the territory, Jingxuan was made Grand Area Commander and Inspector of Yu Province, stationed at Lekou.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing soon rebelled south; to keep Eastern Wei from retaking the region, Jingxuan was named grand area commander and inspector of Yu Province, with his seat at Lekou.

sentences.zh: 東魏亦遣張伯德為刺史。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei also sent Zhang Bode as inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei appointed Zhang Bode inspector in turn.

sentences.zh: 伯德令其將劉貴平率其戍卒及山蠻，屢來攻逼。

translations.literal: Bode had his general Liu Guiping lead garrison troops and mountain barbarians, repeatedly coming to attack and press.
translations.idiomatic: Bode sent Liu Guiping at the head of garrison soldiers and mountain tribesmen to harry him again and again.

sentences.zh: 景宣兵不滿千人，隨機奮擊，前後擒斬三千餘級，貴平乃退走。

translations.literal: Jingxuan's troops numbered less than a thousand; he struck fiercely as occasion allowed, capturing and beheading more than three thousand in all, and Guiping then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: With fewer than a thousand men Jingxuan counterattacked whenever he saw an opening, killing or capturing more than three thousand over time until Guiping pulled back.

sentences.zh: 進授使持節、車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: Advanced and granted acting staff of authority, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Honor Equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted and given acting staff of authority, the rank of general of chariots and cavalry, and honor equal to the three excellencies.

sentences.zh: 潁川陷後，太祖以樂口等諸城道路阻絕，悉令拔還。

translations.literal: After Yingchuan fell, the Grand Progenitor, because roads to Lekou and other cities were cut off, ordered all to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yingchuan was lost, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai, finding the routes to Lekou and the other strongpoints severed, ordered a general pullback.

sentences.zh: 襄州刺史杞秀以狼狽得罪。

translations.literal: Inspector of Xiang Province Qi Xiu was punished for disgraceful failure.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Xiu, inspector of Xiang Province, was condemned for a shameful rout.

sentences.zh: 景宣號令嚴明，戎旅整肅，所部全濟，獨被優賞。

translations.literal: Jingxuan's commands were strict and clear, his troops orderly; his command came through intact and he alone received exceptional reward.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan kept tight discipline and brought his force home whole, and he alone won special commendation.

sentences.zh: 仍留鎮荊州，委以鵶南之事。

translations.literal: He remained to garrison Jing Province, entrusted with the affairs of Yan-nan.
translations.idiomatic: He stayed on in Jing Province, charged with affairs south of the Han River.

sentences.zh: 初，梁岳陽王蕭詧將以襄陽歸朝，仍勒兵攻梁元帝於江陵。

translations.literal: Initially, Liang's Prince of Yueyang Xiao Cha was about to submit Xiangyang to the court, yet still mobilized troops to attack Liang's Emperor Yuan at Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: At first the Liang prince of Yueyang, Xiao Cha, meant to bring Xiangyang over to the Zhou court even while he marched against Emperor Yuan at Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 詧叛將杜岸乘虛襲之。

translations.literal: Cha's turncoat general Du An took advantage of the opening to strike him.
translations.idiomatic: Cha's defector Du An seized the moment and struck at him.

sentences.zh: 景宣乃率騎三千，助詧破岸。

translations.literal: Jingxuan then led three thousand cavalry to help Cha defeat An.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan rode in with three thousand horse, helped Cha break Du An, and saved the day.

sentences.zh: 詧因是乃送其妻王氏及子嶚入質。

translations.literal: Cha therefore sent his wife Lady Wang and son Yao as hostages.
translations.idiomatic: Grateful, Cha sent his wife Lady Wang and his son Yao as hostages.

sentences.zh: 景宣又與開府楊忠取梁將柳仲禮，拔安陸、隨郡。

translations.literal: Jingxuan again with Opening-establishment Yang Zhong captured Liang general Liu Zhongli and took Anlu and Suichun.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan then joined Yang Zhong, holder of an opening establishment, to capture the Liang general Liu Zhongli and take Anlu and Suichun.

sentences.zh: 久之，隨州城民吳士英等殺刺史黃道玉，因聚為寇。

translations.literal: After some time, Suizhou city dwellers Wu Shiying and others killed the inspector Huang Daoyu and gathered as bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Some time later the Suizhou townsman Wu Shiying and his fellows murdered Inspector Huang Daoyu and raised a band.

sentences.zh: 景宣以英等小賊，可以計取之，若聲其罪，恐同惡者衆。

translations.literal: Jingxuan considered Ying and the others small bandits who could be taken by stratagem; if he proclaimed their crimes, he feared many would share their guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan judged them petty rebels who could be trapped by guile; a public accusation, he thought, would only rally more malcontents.

sentences.zh: 乃與英書，偽稱道玉兇暴，歸功英等。

translations.literal: He then wrote Ying a letter, falsely claiming Daoyu was brutal and crediting Ying and the others.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote to Wu Shiying, pretending that Daoyu had been a tyrant and praising the killers as righteous.

sentences.zh: 英果信之，遂相率而至。

translations.literal: Ying indeed believed it, and they came one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Shiying swallowed the story and led his men in to meet him.

sentences.zh: 景宣執而戮之，散其黨與。

translations.literal: Jingxuan seized and executed them, and dispersed their followers.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan arrested and executed them, then broke up their band.

sentences.zh: 進攻應城，拔之，獲夏侯珍洽。

translations.literal: He advanced to attack Yingcheng, took it, and captured Xiahou Zhenqia.
translations.idiomatic: He pushed on to Yingcheng, captured it, and took Xiahou Zhenqia prisoner.

sentences.zh: 於是應、禮、安、隨並平。

translations.literal: Then Ying, Li, An, and Sui were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Ying, Li, An, and Sui were all brought to order.

sentences.zh: 朝議以景宣威行南服，乃授幷安肆郢新應六州諸軍事、幷州刺史。

translations.literal: The court deliberated that Jingxuan's authority extended through the southern domains, and appointed him commander over the six provinces Bing, An, Si, Ying, Xin, and Ying, and Inspector of Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: The court, noting his sway in the south, put him in command of military affairs across Bing, An, Si, Ying, Xin, and Ying and made him inspector of Bing Province.

sentences.zh: 尋進驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，加侍中，兼督江北司二州諸軍事，進爵為伯，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: Soon advanced to General of Fast Cavalry, Opening-establishment Honor Equal to the Three Excellencies, with added Attendant-in-Ordinary, concurrently commanding the two Si provinces north of the Yangtze, advanced in rank to Count with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to general of fast cavalry and opening-establishment honor equal to the three excellencies, made attendant-in-ordinary, given concurrent command of the two Si provinces north of the Yangtze, and raised to count with five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 唐州蠻田魯嘉自號豫州伯，引致齊兵，大為民患。

translations.literal: Tang Province Man Tian Lujia styled himself Count of Yu Province, drew in Qi troops, and greatly harmed the people.
translations.idiomatic: In Tang Province the Man chieftain Tian Lujia called himself count of Yu Province, called in Northern Qi armies, and terrorized the countryside.

sentences.zh: 景宣又破之，獲魯嘉，以其地為郡。

translations.literal: Jingxuan again defeated him, captured Lujia, and made his territory into a commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan defeated him again, seized Lujia, and organized his lands as a new commandery.

sentences.zh: 轉安州刺史。

translations.literal: Transferred to Inspector of An Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to inspector of An Province.

sentences.zh: 梁定州刺史李洪遠初款後叛，景宣惡其懷貳，密襲破之，虜其家口及部衆。

translations.literal: Liang's Inspector of Ding Province Li Hongyuan at first submitted then rebelled; Jingxuan hated his double-mindedness, secretly struck and broke him, and captured his family and followers.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongyuan, Liang inspector of Ding Province, had first submitted and then rebelled; disgusted by his wavering, Jingxuan launched a surprise attack, crushed him, and took his household and troops captive.

sentences.zh: 洪遠脫身走免。

translations.literal: Hongyuan escaped by himself and got away.
translations.idiomatic: Hongyuan alone slipped free and fled.

sentences.zh: 自是酋帥懾服，無敢叛者。

translations.literal: From then on tribal chiefs were awed into submission, and none dared rebel.
translations.idiomatic: After that the frontier chiefs submitted in fear, and no one dared revolt again.

sentences.zh: 燕公于謹征江陵，景宣別破梁司空陸法和司馬羊亮於溳水。

translations.literal: Duke of Yan Yu Jin campaigned against Jiangling; Jingxuan separately defeated Liang's Minister of Works Lu Fazhe and Marshal Yang Liang at the Yun River.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke of Yan Yu Jin marched on Jiangling, Jingxuan on a separate front routed Liang minister of works Lu Fazhe and marshal Yang Liang on the Yun River.

sentences.zh: 又遣別帥攻拔魯山。

translations.literal: He again sent a separate commander to attack and take Lushan.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent a detached force to capture Lushan.

sentences.zh: 多造舟艦，益張旗幟，臨江欲度，以懼梁人。

translations.literal: He built many boats and ships, spread more banners and flags, and faced the river intending to cross, to frighten the Liang people.
translations.idiomatic: He massed boats, raised extra banners along the bank, and feigned a crossing to intimidate the Liang forces.

sentences.zh: 梁將王琳在湘州，景宣遺之書，諭以禍福。

translations.literal: Liang general Wang Lin was in Xiang Province; Jingxuan sent him a letter, expounding fortune and disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lin, a Liang general in Xiang Province, received a letter from Jingxuan laying out the costs of resistance and the rewards of submission.

sentences.zh: 琳遂遣長史席壑因景宣請舉州款附。

translations.literal: Lin then sent his chief clerk Xi He through Jingxuan to request that the whole province submit.
translations.idiomatic: Lin answered by sending his chief clerk Xi He via Jingxuan to offer the province's surrender.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，徵為司憲中大夫，尋除基鄀硤平四州五防諸軍事、江陵防主，加大將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, he was summoned as Central Grandee of the Ministry of Justice; soon appointed commander of the five defenses of the four provinces Ji, E, Xia, and Ping, Warden of Jiangling defenses, with added Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin succeeded, Jingxuan was recalled as central grandee of the ministry of justice, then made commander of the five garrisons of Ji, E, Xia, and Ping, warden of Jiangling's defenses, and grand general.

sentences.zh: 保定四年，晉公護東討，景宣別討河南。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Baoding, Duke of Jin Hu campaigned east; Jingxuan separately campaigned in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoding year 4, while Yuwen Hu, Duke of Jin, marched east, Jingxuan led a separate drive into Henan.

sentences.zh: 齊豫州刺史王士良、永州刺史蕭世怡並以城降。

translations.literal: Qi Inspectors of Yu Province Wang Shiliang and Yong Province Xiao Shiyi both surrendered their cities.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shiliang, Qi inspector of Yu Province, and Xiao Shiyi, inspector of Yong Province, both handed over their cities.

sentences.zh: 景宣以開府謝徹守永州，開府郭彥守豫州，以士良、世怡及降卒一千人歸諸京師。

translations.literal: Jingxuan had Opening-establishment Xie Che hold Yong Province and Opening-establishment Guo Yan hold Yu Province, and sent Shiliang, Shiyi, and one thousand surrendered soldiers to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan left Xie Che to hold Yong Province and Guo Yan to hold Yu Province, then sent Shiliang, Shiyi, and a thousand surrendered troops to the capital.

sentences.zh: 尋而洛陽不守，乃棄二州，拔其將士而還。

translations.literal: Before long Luoyang could not be held; he abandoned the two provinces and withdrew his generals and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang soon fell; he gave up both provinces and pulled his officers and men back.

sentences.zh: 至昌州而羅陽蠻反，景宣回軍破之，斬首千級，獲生口二千、雜畜千頭，送闕。

translations.literal: On reaching Chang Province the Luoyang Man rebelled; Jingxuan turned his army, defeated them, beheaded a thousand, captured two thousand living persons and a thousand mixed livestock, and sent them to the court.
translations.idiomatic: At Chang Province the Luoyang tribes rose; Jingxuan wheeled about, crushed them, took a thousand heads, two thousand captives, and a thousand head of livestock, and sent the spoils to court.

sentences.zh: 還次灞上，晉公護親迎勞之。

translations.literal: On return he halted at Bashang; Duke of Jin Hu personally came to welcome and comfort him.
translations.idiomatic: On the march home he stopped at Bashang, where Yuwen Hu came out in person to greet and reward him.

sentences.zh: 天和初，授荊州總管、十七州諸軍事、荊州刺史，進爵千金郡公。

translations.literal: At the start of Tianhe, appointed Grand Governor of Jing Province with command over seventeen provinces' military affairs and Inspector of Jing Province, advanced to Duke of Qianjin Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Tianhe he became grand governor of Jing Province with authority over seventeen provinces, inspector of Jing, and duke of Qianjin commandery.

sentences.zh: 陳湘州刺史華皎舉州款附，表請援兵。

translations.literal: Chen's Inspector of Xiang Province Hua Jiao offered the province in submission and memorialized requesting relief troops.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Jiao, Chen inspector of Xiang Province, surrendered his province and asked for reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 勑景宣統水軍與皎俱下。

translations.literal: An imperial order directed Jingxuan to command the water army and go downriver with Jiao.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered Jingxuan to take the river fleet and descend with Jiao.

sentences.zh: 景宣到夏口，陳人已至。

translations.literal: Jingxuan reached Xiakou; Chen troops had already arrived.
translations.idiomatic: By the time Jingxuan reached Xiakou, Chen forces were already there.

sentences.zh: 而景宣以任遇隆重，遂驕傲恣縱，多自矜伐，兼納賄貨，指麾節度，朝出夕改。

translations.literal: But Jingxuan, because his appointment and favor were weighty, then grew proud and unrestrained, often praising himself, and also accepted bribes; his commands changed morning to evening.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Jingxuan, swollen by his high rank and favor, turned arrogant and loose, bragged of his deeds, took bribes, and changed his orders from morning to night.

sentences.zh: 將士憤怒，莫肯用命。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers were angry and none would obey orders.
translations.idiomatic: His officers and men seethed with resentment and refused to follow him.

sentences.zh: 及水軍始交，一時奔北，船艦器仗，略無孑遺。

translations.literal: When the water armies first clashed, they fled north all at once; boats, weapons, and gear were nearly all lost.
translations.idiomatic: At the first contact on the water they broke and ran; ships, arms, and equipment were almost entirely lost.

sentences.zh: 時衛公直總督諸軍，以景宣負敗，欲繩以軍法。

translations.literal: At the time Duke of Wei Yu Zhi commanded all armies; because Jingxuan had failed, he wished to punish him by military law.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zhi, Duke of Wei, then commanded the whole force and wanted Jingxuan court-martialed for the defeat.

sentences.zh: 朝廷不忍加罪，遣使就軍赦之。

translations.literal: The court could not bear to punish him and sent an envoy to the army to pardon him.
translations.idiomatic: The court shrank from condemning him and dispatched an envoy to the camp to grant a pardon.

sentences.zh: 尋遇疾卒。

translations.literal: Before long he fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: He soon sickened and died.

sentences.zh: 贈河渭鄯三州刺史，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: Posthumously honored as Inspector of the three provinces He, Wei, and Shan; posthumous title Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made inspector of He, Wei, and Shan provinces and given the posthumous name Gong.

sentences.zh: 子如璋嗣。

translations.literal: His son Ruzhang succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ruzhang inherited the line.

sentences.zh: 位至開府、膠州刺史。

translations.literal: He reached Opening-establishment and Inspector of Jiao Province.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to opening-establishment rank and the inspectorate of Jiao Province.

sentences.zh: 如璋弟如玖，儀同大將軍、廣川縣侯。

translations.literal: Ruzhang's younger brother Rujiu, General Honor Equal to the Three Excellencies and Marquis of Guangchuan County.
translations.idiomatic: Ruzhang's younger brother Rujiu held the rank of general honor equal to the three excellencies and was marquis of Guangchuan county.

sentences.zh: 景宣之去樂口，南荊州刺史郭賢據魯陽以拒東魏。

translations.literal: When Jingxuan left Leykou, Southern Jing Province Inspector Guo Xian held Luyang to resist Eastern Wei.
translations.idiomatic: After Quan Jingxuan withdrew from Leykou, Guo Xian, inspector of Southern Jing, garrisoned Luyang against Eastern Wei.

sentences.zh: 賢字道因，趙興陽州人也。

translations.literal: Xian, styled Daoyin, was a man of Yang Province in Zhao Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xian, courtesy name Daoyin, came from Yang Province in Zhao Xing commandery.

sentences.zh: 父雲，涼州司馬。

translations.literal: His father Yun was Liangzhou vice-governor.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yun had served as vice-governor of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 賢性強記，學涉經史。

translations.literal: Xian by nature had strong memory; in learning he ranged through the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xian remembered everything he read and had a broad grounding in the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 魏正光末，賊帥宿勤明達圍逼豳州，刺史畢暉補賢統軍，與之拒守。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhenguang of Wei, the bandit chief Suqin Mingda besieged Bin Prefecture; Inspector Bi Hui appointed Xian army commander, and together they held out against him.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Wei's Zhenguang era, the rebel leader Suqin Mingda pressed Bin Prefecture; Bi Hui, the inspector, put Guo Xian in command of the garrison, and together they held the city.

sentences.zh: 後為州主簿，行北地郡事。

translations.literal: Later he became provincial chief clerk and administered Beidi commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as the province's chief clerk and acted as administrator of Beidi commandery.

sentences.zh: 以征討有功，授都督。

translations.literal: For merit in campaigns and suppression, he was granted area commander.
translations.idiomatic: Campaign merit won him the rank of area commander.

sentences.zh: 尋加伏波將軍，從王思政鎮弘農。

translations.literal: Soon he was further made General Who Quells the Waves and followed Wang Sizheng in garrisoning Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to General Who Quells the Waves and followed Wang Sizheng to the Hongnong garrison.

sentences.zh: 授使持節、行義州事、當州都督。

translations.literal: He was granted bearer of the staff, administrator of Yi Prefecture, and area commander of that prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He received the staff of authority, was made acting administrator of Yi Prefecture, and given command over the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 轉行弘農郡事。

translations.literal: Transferred to administer Hongnong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to act as administrator of Hongnong commandery.

sentences.zh: 賢質直有算略，思政甚重之，禦邊之謀，多與賢參決。

translations.literal: Xian was plain and direct yet possessed stratagem; Sizheng greatly valued him, and in plans for defending the frontier he often consulted Xian in decision.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xian was blunt but shrewd; Wang Sizheng relied on him heavily, and most frontier strategy passed through his counsel.

sentences.zh: 十二年，除輔國將軍、南〔荊〕州刺史。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, appointed General Who Supports the State, South 〔Jing〕 [emended variant] Prefecture inspector.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was appointed General Who Supports the State and inspector of Southern Jing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 及侯景來附，思政遣賢先出三鵶，鎮於魯陽。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing came to submit, Sizheng sent Xian ahead to Three Geese and garrisoned at Luyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing defected, Wang Sizheng sent Guo Xian forward to Three Geese and posted him at Luyang.

sentences.zh: 加大都督，封安武縣子，邑四百戶。

translations.literal: Added grand area commander; enfeoffed as Baron of Anwu county with a fief of four hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was made grand area commander and enfeoffed Baron of Anwu with four hundred households.

sentences.zh: 尋進車騎大將軍、儀同三司，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Soon advanced to Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Equal in Protocol to the Three Excellencies, with Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary added.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon raised to Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, equal-in-protocol to the Three Excellencies, with the added title Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 及潁川被圍，東魏遣蠻酋魯和扇動群蠻，規斷囗路。

translations.literal: When Yingchuan was besieged, Eastern Wei sent the barbarian chieftain Lu He to stir up the tribal groups and plan to cut the □ supply route.
translations.idiomatic: While Yingchuan was under siege, Eastern Wei sent the tribal chief Lu He to rouse the barbarians and try to sever the grain route.

sentences.zh: 和乃遣其從弟與和為漢廣郡守，率其部曲，侵擾州境。

translations.literal: He then sent his younger cousin Yu He to be governor of Hanguang commandery, leading his personal troops to raid the prefecture's borders.
translations.idiomatic: Lu He then put his cousin Yu He in charge of Hanguang commandery and sent his own followers to harry the province.

sentences.zh: 賢密簡士馬，輕往掩襲，大破之，遂擒魯和。

translations.literal: Xian secretly picked elite men and horses, went lightly and made a surprise attack, routed them completely, and thereupon captured Lu He.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xian secretly mustered picked troops, struck by surprise with a light column, broke them utterly, and took Lu He alive.

sentences.zh: 旣而潁川陷，權景宣等並拔軍西還，自魯陽以東，皆附東魏。

translations.literal: Soon Yingchuan fell; Quan Jingxuan and the others all withdrew their armies westward, and from Luyang eastward all submitted to Eastern Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Yingchuan soon fell; Quan Jingxuan and the rest pulled their forces back west, and everything east of Luyang went over to Eastern Wei.

sentences.zh: 〔東魏〕將彭樂因之，遂來攻逼。

translations.literal: 〔Eastern Wei〕 [emended variant] General Peng Le took advantage of this and thereupon came to attack and press.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei general Peng Le seized the moment and marched to attack.

sentences.zh: 賢撫循將士，咸為盡其力用，樂不能克，乃引軍退。

translations.literal: Xian comforted and rallied officers and men; all exerted their strength to the utmost, and Le could not overcome him, then led his army in withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xian steadied his troops until every man fought his hardest; Peng Le failed to break him and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 而東魏又以土民韋默兒為義州刺史，鎮父城以逼賢。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei again made the local clansman Wei Mo'er Yi Prefecture governor and garrisoned Fucheng to press Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei then installed the local leader Wei Mo'er as governor of Yi Prefecture and held Fucheng to threaten Guo Xian.

sentences.zh: 賢又率軍攻默兒，擒之。

translations.literal: Xian again led his army to attack Mo'er and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xian marched out again, attacked Wei Mo'er, and took him prisoner.

sentences.zh: 轉廣州刺史。

translations.literal: Transferred to Guang Prefecture governor.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to governor of Guang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 後從尉遲迥伐蜀，行安州事。

translations.literal: Later he followed Yuchi Jiong in the campaign against Shu and administered An Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed Yuchi Jiong in the conquest of Shu and acted as administrator of An Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 魏恭帝元年，行寧蜀郡事，兼益州長史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Emperor Gong of Wei, he administered Ningshu commandery and concurrently served as senior administrator of Yi Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Emperor Gong of Wei he governed Ningshu commandery while also serving as senior administrator of Yi Province.

sentences.zh: 以平蜀勳，進爵為伯，增邑五百戶。

translations.literal: For merit in pacifying Shu, he advanced in noble rank to baron and his fief was increased by five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Merit in pacifying Shu raised him to baron and added five hundred households to his fief.

sentences.zh: 轉行始州事。

translations.literal: Transferred to administer Shi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to act as administrator of Shi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，進位驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，進爵為侯，增邑通前一千四百戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin ascended the throne, he advanced in rank to Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Opening Office Equal in Protocol to the Three Excellencies, advanced in noble rank to marquis, and his fief was increased to one thousand four hundred households in all.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, Guo Xian rose to Grand General of Agile Cavalry and opening-office equal-in-protocol to the Three Excellencies, was enfeoffed marquis, and his fief reached fourteen hundred households in total.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，除

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Shizong's reign, appointed as
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Shizong's reign he was made

translations.literal: (Ying) [emended: general]
translations.idiomatic: general-master

sentences.zh: 〔匠〕師中大夫。

translations.literal: 〔Jiang〕 [emended: general] master middle grandee.
translations.idiomatic: middle grandee.

sentences.zh: 尋出為勳州刺史，鎮玉壁。

translations.literal: Soon sent out as Xun Prefecture governor, garrisoning Yubi.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon sent out as governor of Xun Prefecture and posted at Yubi.

sentences.zh: 武成二年，遷安應等十二州諸軍事、安州刺史，進爵樂昌縣公。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wucheng, transferred to commander over the twelve prefectures including An and Ying and governor of An Prefecture; advanced in noble rank to Duke of Lechang county.
translations.idiomatic: In Wucheng year 2 he became commander over twelve prefectures including An and Ying and governor of An Prefecture, and was raised to Duke of Lechang.

sentences.zh: 賢在官雖無明察之譽，以廉平待物，去後頗亦見思。

translations.literal: While in office Xian had no reputation for sharp discernment, yet he treated people with integrity and fairness; after he left, many also remembered him with affection.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xian was never famed for keen judgment, but he governed fairly and with restraint, and after his departure people still spoke of him fondly.

sentences.zh: 保定三年，轉陝州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third year of Baoding, transferred to Shan Prefecture governor.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoding year 3 he was transferred to governor of Shan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 天和元年，卒於位。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianhe, he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in Tianhe year 1.

sentences.zh: 贈少保、寧蔚朔三州刺史，諡曰節。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Junior Preceptor and governor of the three provinces Ning, Wei, and Shuo; posthumous title Jie.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made junior preceptor and governor of Ning, Wei, and Shuo provinces, with the posthumous name Jie.

sentences.zh: 賢衣服飲食雖以儉約自處，而居家豐麗，室有餘貲。

translations.literal: Though in dress and food Xian kept himself frugal and sparing, at home he lived in rich splendor and his household had surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xian dressed and ate plainly in public, yet kept a lavish house and ample private means.

sentences.zh: 時論譏其詐云。

translations.literal: Opinion of the time mocked him for deceit, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries, it was said, derided the pretense.

sentences.zh: 子正嗣。

translations.literal: His son Zheng succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng inherited the line.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：昔耿恭抗勁虜於疏勒，馬敦拒羣兵於汧城，雖以生易死，終賴王師之助，其嘉聲峻節，亦見稱於良史焉。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: In old times Geng Gong resisted fierce enemies at Shule, and Ma Dun held off massed troops at Qian city; though they traded life for death, in the end they relied on the royal army's aid—their fine renown and lofty integrity were also praised in good histories.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Long ago Geng Gong held Shule against overwhelming foes and Ma Dun turned back a host at Qian city; both were ready to die, yet both needed the imperial army's rescue before their glory entered the annals.

sentences.zh: 賀若敦志節慷慨，深入敵境，勍敵絕其糧道，長江阻其歸塗，勢危而策出無方，事迫而雄心彌厲。

translations.literal: He Ruodun's resolve and integrity were generous and ardent; he penetrated deep into enemy territory; formidable foes cut his grain route, the Yangtze blocked his road of return; the situation was perilous yet no stratagem issued forth, the crisis pressed yet his bold heart grew fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: He Ruodun was ardent and resolute; he plunged deep into enemy country while strong foes severed his supplies and the Yangtze cut off retreat. Peril closed in with no plan at hand, yet the tighter the crisis, the fiercer his will.

sentences.zh: 故能使士卒感其義，敵人畏其威，利涉死地，全師而返。

translations.literal: Therefore he could make officers and soldiers feel his righteousness, enemies fear his awesomeness, cross deadly ground with profit, and return with the whole army intact.
translations.idiomatic: His men were moved by his example, his enemies cowed by his name; he crossed ground where death waited and brought the whole army home.

sentences.zh: 非夫忘生以徇國者，其孰能若此者乎。

translations.literal: If not one who forgets life to follow the state, who indeed could be like this?
translations.idiomatic: Who but a man ready to die for his country could have done the same?

sentences.zh: 俯窺元定之傳，曾糞土之不若也。

translations.literal: Looking down upon Yuan Ding's biography, he was not even fit to be counted as dung and soil.
translations.idiomatic: Set beside the account of Yuan Ding, He Ruodun was worth more than a heap of dust.

sentences.zh: 誠宜裂地以賞之，分職以授之；

translations.literal: Truly he ought to have been rewarded with carved lands and granted divided offices;
translations.idiomatic: He deserved fiefs cut from the realm and high office commensurate with his deeds;

sentences.zh: 而茂勳莫紀，嚴刑已及。

translations.literal: Yet abundant merit went unrecorded, and severe punishment had already reached him.
translations.idiomatic: yet his towering service went unrewarded while harsh punishment fell on him instead.

sentences.zh: 嗟乎！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Ah, what a pity!

sentences.zh: 政之紕繆，一至於此！

translations.literal: The disorder of governance reached this extreme!
translations.idiomatic: Government had gone so far wrong!

sentences.zh: 天下是以知宇文護不能終其位焉。

translations.literal: All under Heaven thereby knew that Yuwen Hu could not keep his position to the end.
translations.idiomatic: The realm could see from this that Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu would not hold power to the end.

sentences.zh: 史寧、權景宣並以將帥之才，受內外之寵。

translations.literal: Shi Ning and Quan Jingxuan both possessed the talent of generals and received favor within and without.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Ning and Quan Jingxuan were both born commanders and enjoyed favor at court and in the field.

sentences.zh: 總戎薄伐，著剋敵之功；

translations.literal: Commanding armies on brief campaigns, they displayed merit in overcoming the enemy;
translations.idiomatic: Leading troops in swift campaigns, they won clear victories over the foe;

sentences.zh: 布政蒞民，垂稱職之譽。

translations.literal: Spreading governance and presiding over the people, they left reputations of fulfilling their offices.
translations.idiomatic: In civil rule they governed the people well and earned lasting praise for competent service.

sentences.zh: 若此者，豈非有國之良翰歟。

translations.literal: Men such as these—are they not the good pillars of a state?
translations.idiomatic: Were these not precisely the sort of men a state needs as its firm supports?

sentences.zh: 然而史在末年，貨財虧其雅志。

translations.literal: Yet Shi, in his later years, let goods and wealth impair his lofty intent.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in his last years Shi Ning let greed for wealth stain the high purpose of his youth.

sentences.zh: 權亦晚節矜驕，喪其威聲。

translations.literal: Quan likewise in late life grew proud and arrogant, losing his awesomeness and renown.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Jingxuan, too, turned arrogant in old age and forfeited the authority his name had once carried.

sentences.zh: 傳曰「終之實難」，其斯之謂矣。

translations.literal: The Classic says, "Ending well is indeed hard"—this is what it speaks of.
translations.idiomatic: As the Classic says, "To finish well is the hard part"—exactly that.

sentences.zh: 陸騰志氣懍然，雅仗名節。

translations.literal: Lu Teng's spirit and resolve were stern; he nobly relied on reputation and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Teng's bearing was austere and he lived by name and principle.

sentences.zh: 及授戎律，建藩麾，席捲巴梁，則功著銘典；

translations.literal: When he received military law and raised a frontier banner, sweeping through Ba and Liang, then his merit was recorded in inscribed canons;
translations.idiomatic: Once he took command and raised his standard on the frontier, rolling through Ba and Liang, his achievements were fit to be cut in stone;

sentences.zh: 雲撤江漢，則聲流帝籍。

translations.literal: When clouds withdrew from Jiang and Han, then his fame flowed into the imperial registers.
translations.idiomatic: and when peace spread over the Jiang and Han, his renown entered the court's records.

sentences.zh: 身名俱劭，其最優乎。

translations.literal: Person and name both strong—is he not the foremost among them?
translations.idiomatic: In life and in fame alike he stood foremost—was he not the best of them all?

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七一年十一月版《周書》為本校。

translations.literal: The entire text uses the Zhonghua Shuju, November 1971 edition of the Book of Zhou, as the base for this collation.
translations.idiomatic: This text was collated against the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the 《Book of Zhou》 (November 1971).
